articles.title: Crypto Today: tablecoin Savings, Solana, OpenAI
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, a new report highlighted substantial cost savings from stablecoin remittances, especially in emerging markets. Meanwhile, Solana postponed its Shanghai event after registrations exceeded local capacity limits and an OpenAI research model accessed a crypto wallet without authorization to deploy smart contracts.
Stablecoin remittances cost 84% less than traditional transfers, Borderless finds
Stablecoin-funded remittances cost roughly 84% less than traditional money transfers, according to a new third-quarter report from payments network Borderless.xyz.
Sending $200 through stablecoin payment networks costs a median of $2, or 1%, compared with $12.72, or 6.36%, for conventional remittances. The comparison uses Borderless pricing from the third quarter of 2026 and World Bank data from the same period last year.
Savings were particularly pronounced in emerging markets. In Sub-Saharan Africa, stablecoin remittances cost 2.9%, compared with 8.46% for traditional transfers. In Latin America, the respective costs were 1.25% and 5.64%.
Businesses also stand to benefit. A $10,000 stablecoin-funded transfer to the eurozone costs as little as $26, compared with $135 to $150 for an international bank wire, including foreign-exchange costs.
Stablecoin payouts also settled faster in several markets, with a median of two minutes in Brazil and Colombia and three minutes in Mexico. Traditional SWIFT transfers typically settled the next business day.
However, reliability varied. Payment completion rates reached 98.6% in Mexico but fell to 73% in Costa Rica, highlighting differences in local payment infrastructure.
Solana’s Liu says Shanghai event postponed over registration surge
The Solana Accelerate event in Shanghai was postponed after pre-registration exceeded the event cap set by local authorities, according to Lily Liu, president of the Solana Foundation.
Event registration quadrupled overnight following publicity for the event, Liu wrote in a Friday X post, adding that organizers decided to postpone the event to “comply with local requirements.”
Earlier on Friday, X users claimed that the event was “abruptly suspended” as law enforcement officers were stationed at the venue.
In October 2025, a Solana event in Shenzhen was also cut short due to venue capacity and public-safety concerns, Solana’s Chinese-language community account announced then on X.
Shanghai was scheduled to open Solana’s four-city Accelerate China tour, followed by Hangzhou on Sunday, Shenzhen on Tuesday and Beijing on Thursday, according to the event’s website.
The postponement followed Solana executives’ promotion of a new Shanghai office earlier this week.
OpenAI model helped itself to testnet crypto, then kept quiet about it
An internal research model at OpenAI accessed a funded crypto wallet without authorization, using testnet Ether to deploy smart contracts on the Sepolia network and later omitting the spending from its final task summary.
OpenAI said the model, which was part of its GPT-5.6 Sol family, was given the task of updating a crypto trading prototype and deploying compatible contracts. After failing to obtain testnet ETH through faucets, the model derived accounts from publicly known developer recovery phrases, checked 362 wallet addresses and selected one with enough funds to proceed.
In its recorded reasoning, the model asked, “But using public known key/funds ethically?” It then argued that the funds were “effectively abandoned/test ETH” and that Sepolia ETH had no value, before using the wallet’s private key to sign and broadcast a deployment transaction. The transaction succeeded, with fees charged to the account.
OpenAI said the incident showed how an AI model could decide on its own that using someone else’s funds was acceptable, even without permission. The company discovered the incident while reviewing earlier model activity and has since introduced safeguards to prevent live internet access in similar situations.

articles.title: Hackers Jailbreak iPhone 18 Pro on Stage, and It Survives a Reboot - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Calif showed an untethered iOS 27.0.1 jailbreak on an iPhone 18 Pro at Hexacon in Paris on October 16, with root access returning after a reboot.
- The firm has not named the vulnerabilities or released a tool, and says it will publish everything later.
- Apple's iOS 27 security notes credit Calif.io, working with Claude and Anthropic Research, for two unrelated crash bugs; Apple has not commented on the demo.
Security firm Calif.io demonstrated an untethered jailbreak on an iPhone 18 Pro running iOS 27.0.1 on stage at Hexacon, the offensive security conference in Paris, on Friday. It's the first time an untethered, permanent jailbreak is successful in such devices.
A jailbreak strips away Apple's software restrictions, and untethered means it comes back on its own after a restart, with no computer attached.
Apple builds the iPhone as a locked-down system, with signed code, a sandbox around every app and a protected startup chain, so owners cannot change how iOS works or run software the company has not allowed. A jailbreak breaks that lock and hands the user root access, which lets them install apps Apple never approved, add new features, customize the interface and use the phone in ways Apple did not intend.
For example, back in the early iOS days, users with jailbroken phones were capable of filming video before Apple shipped that feature. They were also able to run Android on their iPhones, unlock carriers, install themes, and so on. Right now a user with a jailbroken iPhone can install apps outside of the Appstore, browse the full file system and delete bloatware.
Few people do this today, but every working jailbreak on current hardware shows that the defenses Apple invests heavily in can still be beaten.
Video from the stage, posted by jailbreak researcher Billy Ellis, shows the team rebooting the phone, unlocking it with the regular passcode and opening an SSH session as root, the highest level of access on the device. The terminal output listed iOS 27.0.1 and an uptime of about two minutes.
At #hexacon - https://t.co/jEOpspETlT demos iOS 27.0.1 untethered jailbreak on iPhone 18 Pro pic.twitter.com/S54aRrzHFS
— Billy Ellis (@bellis1000) October 16, 2026
Hexacon runs October 16 and 17 in Paris, so the demo came on the opening day of the conference. The event is aimed at researchers who find and exploit security flaws, and its talks typically cover bugs in widely used platforms such as phones and browsers.
Calif has not said which vulnerabilities it used, and no public tool exists. Its newsletter post from the conference lists four demos, including a Signal one-click and an iMessage demo, and says everything “will be released in due time.”
3/ Can your iPhone do this? pic.twitter.com/gT0Z781Tnl
— Calif (@calif_io) October 16, 2026
Getting root on a current iPhone usually takes a chain of bugs that escapes the app sandbox, takes over the kernel and gets past hardware-backed defenses such as Pointer Authentication Codes, which detect tampering with memory pointers. Surviving a reboot is harder still, because Apple checks the code that runs at startup.
In April, Calif's Thai Duong wrote that Claude helped him take apart an iOS Safari exploit, in a series on how a real iPhone jailbreak works. In May, Calif said Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview helped it build a macOS kernel exploit against Apple's M5 chip protections in under a week.
“We didn’t build the chain alone. Mythos Preview helped identify the bugs and assisted throughout exploit development,” he said.
Apple's iOS 27 security notes, published September 14, credit Calif.io “in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research” for two bugs that let an app cause a denial of service or a system crash. Nothing in the notes ties either bug to the jailbreak.
A chain that gives root on a fully updated iPhone is the same kind of capability that commercial spyware vendors sell to governments, and Apple usually patches such chains once it learns the details. How long iOS 27.0.1 stays exposed therefore depends largely on when Calif chooses to publish.
Apple has not publicly commented on the demo as of Friday, and says it does not confirm security issues until patches are available. Calif has not said when it will publish the details.

articles.title: Crypto-Aligned PACs Pour $52M into Opposing Sherrod Brown in Ohio
articles.text:
Crypto PACs escalate spending against Sherrod Brown in Ohio Senate race
At least two industry-aligned PACs have poured more than $52 million into opposing Sherrod Brown’s return to the Senate.
Affiliates of the Fairshake political action committee (PAC), largely funded by Coinbase and Ripple Labs, have increased their initially announced expenditures by more than 50% in what could be a key race for control of Congress in 2026.
According to Thursday filings with the Federal Election Commission (FEC), the Fairshake affiliate Defend American Jobs — a group that supports Republican candidates in primaries and elections — spent $46.6 million on media opposing former lawmaker Sherrod Brown and supporting Republican incumbent Jon Husted in Ohio’s Senate race for the 2026 midterms. The spending marked a sharp increase over what Fairshake said in September it initially planned to spend opposing Brown’s return to the Senate: $30 million.
“I’ve spent my career taking on Wall Street, taking on big pharma, taking on big oil and been successful in many cases,” said Brown in an interview aired Friday on Pod Save America, addressing the attack ads funded by the crypto industry, adding:
“Jon Husted is their boy [...] They know he’s their guy, they know I’m going to hold him accountable and I guess it’s a perfect storm, so they spend literally tens and tens of millions of dollars.”
With just under three weeks until the US election, early voting has already been underway for 10 days in Ohio. Notably, Fairshake’s affiliate was not the only crypto-aligned PAC to ramp up spending as Ohio voters cast their ballots. The Digital Freedom Fund, a Super PAC created by Gemini co-founders Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss, reported about $3 million in ad spending this week to oppose Brown and support Husted, bringing the group’s total media purchases in the Ohio race to more than $5.9 million.
Fairshake’s expenditures have already exceeded its efforts in 2024, when the PAC spent $41 million supporting Republican Bernie Moreno and opposing Brown, who was running for reelection to the Senate at the time. The Democratic lawmaker chaired the Senate Banking Committee and was one of the more outspoken voices challenging laws and policies favored by the crypto industry while serving in Congress.
Related: Vivek Ramaswamy’s gubernatorial run lacks the crypto rhetoric of his presidential bid
The Ohio race isn’t Fairshake’s only focus with the midterm elections looming. Defend American Jobs reported spending more than $6.7 million to oppose Independent candidate Dan Osborn in Nebraska’s Senate race. Osborn is running against Republican Pete Ricketts, who voted in favor of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act and the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act while in office.
Cointelegraph reached out to Fairshake and Husted’s campaign for comment but did not receive an immediate response.
How could the 2026 elections shape US crypto laws and policy?
Fairshake has been open about its intention to “back pro-crypto candidates” in 2026 as part of a goal to fill the next session of Congress with lawmakers supportive of policies favored by the industry. The PAC reported in January that it held $193 million in cash on hand ahead of the elections.
Beyond PACs like Fairshake and Digital Freedom Fund, other groups aligned with crypto interests have already tried to influence 2026 voters. The Fellowship committee, backed by Cantor Fitzgerald and Anchorage Digital, reported spending more than $11 million between August 2025 and August 2026, largely on media supporting House and Senate candidates.
Magazine: Can the SEC and CFTC’s pro-crypto rules be overturned? Legal opinion

articles.title: Circle Plans Push Into 40 Emerging Markets as Stablecoins Go Mainstream, CEO Says - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Circle plans to expand into roughly 40 emerging and developing countries, CEO Jeremy Allaire told Reuters, saying blockchain is entering its “mainstream scaling phase.”
- USDC holds about 25% of the stablecoin market versus roughly 60% for Tether’s USDT, and its circulation rose 19% year over year to $73.3 billion in the second quarter.
- Allaire called the GENIUS Act, set to take effect in January, “a watershed moment,” but warned that AI is heightening security risks.
Circle wants USDC in a lot more wallets around the world.
The stablecoin issuer is preparing to enter roughly 40 emerging and developing countries, CEO Jeremy Allaire told Reuters on the sidelines of the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok.
Allaire pointed to rising organic demand for stablecoins across Southeast Asia, Latin America, Africa, and the Middle East from people and businesses looking to tap into an internet-based economy.
The technology, he said, is moving “from the early adopter phase of blockchain technology into the mainstream scaling phase.”
Stablecoins are cryptocurrencies pegged to a traditional asset, usually the U.S. dollar. Circle’s USDC holds about 25% of the stablecoin market, compared with roughly 60% for Tether’s USDT. USDC’s circulation rose 19% year over year to $73.3 billion in the second quarter.
Circle has resources for the push, including its $400 million acquisition of payments firm Tazapay and a $100 million strategic investment from Binance, Reuters reported.
The company is also leaning on regulatory tailwinds. Circle secured a federal banking charter in July, sending its stock higher, and has pursued a New York trust charter. The GENIUS Act, the U.S. stablecoin law, is slated to take effect in January. Allaire said the law would give the world “legal digital dollars,” calling it “a watershed moment.”
Banks are building their own stablecoins, which Allaire framed as healthy competition. After a long stretch in which incumbents kept outsiders out, he said, “they are no longer in charge, and the innovators are having their day.”
Allaire also credited AI agents making tiny machine-to-machine payments with boosting USDC usage. Circle’s Arc network has been adopted by BlackRock, Visa and Standard Chartered, according to Reuters. Circle has been pushing to make USDC the currency of AI agents.
But Allaire warned that AI also raises security risks for financial infrastructure. “If you’re not concerned about it, then your head is in the sand, right?” he said.

articles.title: Stablecoin Remittances Offer Major Cost Savings: Report
articles.text:
Stablecoin remittances cost 84% less than traditional transfers, report finds
Borderless.xyz data shows major savings on cross-border business payments, with stablecoin transfers also settling faster than traditional international bank wires.
Stablecoin-funded remittances continue to offer substantial cost savings over traditional money transfers, particularly in emerging markets, reinforcing one of the leading use cases for digital dollars as payment activity grows.
According to a new third-quarter report from Borderless.xyz, a stablecoin payments network, sending a $200 remittance through stablecoin-funded payment rails costs a median of 1%, or $2, compared with 6.36%, or $12.72, for traditional remittances, based on World Bank data.
The difference makes stablecoin-funded remittances roughly 84% cheaper, although the comparison uses Borderless’s third-quarter 2026 pricing and World Bank figures from the same period in 2025.
The savings are also substantial across emerging markets. In Sub-Saharan Africa, stablecoin-funded remittances cost 2.9%, compared with 8.46% for traditional transfers. In Latin America, the costs are 1.25% and 5.64%, respectively.
Business payments made through stablecoins are also significantly cheaper, according to the report. A $10,000 stablecoin-funded transfer to the eurozone costs as little as $26 when routed through the lowest-cost provider, compared with $52 across all corridors at the median provider.
By comparison, a traditional international bank wire costs between $135 and $150 for the same amount, including transfer fees and an assumed 1% foreign-exchange margin.
Stablecoins offer significant cost savings on larger business transactions. Source: Borderless.xyz
Related: Mastercard brings stablecoin balances into traditional banking and card payments
Stablecoin payouts settle in minutes, but reliability varies
Beyond cost savings, the Borderless report found that stablecoin-funded payments can reach recipients’ local bank accounts in minutes, depending on the payment network used.
In Brazil, payouts through the PIX network settled in a median of two minutes during the third quarter, while Mexico’s SPEI network took three minutes. Colombia’s PSE network also recorded a median settlement time of two minutes.
By comparison, traditional SWIFT transfers typically settled the next business day, with the slowest 10% taking three business days.
However, payment completion rates varied considerably. Mexico’s SPEI network successfully completed 98.6% of payouts, followed by Brazil’s PIX at 97.8%. Colombia’s PSE network completed 79%, while Costa Rica’s SINPE recorded a completion rate of just 73%.
The findings come as stablecoin transaction activity continues to grow. Standard Chartered recently highlighted rising transaction volumes despite relatively flat growth in the overall stablecoin market capitalization this year. The bank expects the market to reach $2 trillion by 2030, two years later than its previous forecast.
Related: Crypto Biz: Wealthy investors are buying crypto, but their advisers aren’t sold

articles.title: Bitcoin Treasury Giant Strategy Faces Index Removal Under Finalized MSCI Rules - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- MSCI finalized a rule treating “non-operating companies” as ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes, effective Nov. 30, using a core screen plus a five-ratio exclusion test.
- The change targets Bitcoin treasury firms like Strategy and Metaplanet whose balance sheets are dominated by crypto, and scraps a temporary 2025 reprieve for companies with 50%+ digital-asset holdings; the affected list comes Nov. 11.
- Removal would force index-tracking funds to sell the shares; Saylor called the rule “discriminatory
MSCI has finalized a rule change that threatens to boot Bitcoin treasury companies like Michael Saylor’s Strategy from its widely tracked equity indexes, a move that could cut off a significant source of passive investment demand for their shares.
In an announcement dated Oct. 15, the index provider said it will treat “non-operating companies” as ineligible for inclusion in the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes, implementing a proposal it floated in August with minor modifications. The change takes effect at the close of Nov. 30 as part of MSCI’s November index review.
The new methodology screens for corporate issuers that lack substantial operating assets and behave more like passive investment vehicles than real businesses. Companies that fail an initial “core screen” are then run through an exclusion test based on five financial ratios; a stock gets flagged as ineligible if it trips four or more of them.
The rule is aimed squarely at firms whose balance sheets are dominated by a single asset, the model pioneered by Saylor’s Strategy, which holds hundreds of thousands of Bitcoin, and adopted by Japan’s Metaplanet and a wave of imitators.
To limit index churn, MSCI built in buffers: current index constituents will only be removed if they fail the screen in each of their two most recent annual filing periods, while new additions are blocked if they fail in either of the last two. MSCI said it would publish the final list of affected companies on Nov. 11.
The decision also ends a temporary reprieve. As the crypto-treasury trend exploded, MSCI last year froze certain index adjustments for companies whose digital-asset holdings made up 50% or more of their total assets; that interim measure now gets scrapped, with all such firms assessed under the new rules.
Removal from major MSCI indexes would force the funds that track them to sell the affected shares, potentially pressuring stock prices and shrinking the premium these companies have long traded at over the value of their crypto. Saylor had urged MSCI to drop what he called a “discriminatory” rule that would delete Strategy from its benchmarks.
The threat has already spurred defensive maneuvers. Metaplanet recently sold 10,000 Bitcoin and bought back 11,000 to demonstrate active treasury management, while Strategy has kept accumulating, adding to its stack even as the index question loomed.

articles.title: Crypto Biz: Tokenized Stocks Gain Traction After Hours
articles.text:
Crypto Biz: Wall Street closes at 4. Tokenized stocks keep trading
Tokenized stocks are drawing trading activity beyond Wall Street hours, while Bitcoin miners confront costly AI expansion and new accounting rules could benefit stablecoins.
Tokenization is beginning to reshape traditional financial markets, with stocks increasingly in focus. Much of the attention has centered on the $3.3 billion in tokenized equities now onchain, according to RWA.xyz, but one of the biggest innovations may be what happens before Wall Street opens and after it closes.
According to the latest industry data, more than 70% of tokenized stock trading volume on BNB Chain now occurs outside regular US market hours, with similar patterns emerging on Solana and Base.
Tokenized equities allow investors to trade US stocks across time zones without waiting for Wall Street’s opening bell, potentially changing how liquidity is distributed throughout the day.
However, many platforms driving this activity remain off-limits to American investors, even as US regulators begin to make room for tokenized stock trading.
This week’s Crypto Biz looks at tokenized stock trading, the economics of Bitcoin mining, proposed accounting rules that could make it easier for companies to treat stablecoins as cash equivalents, and Strive’s expanding Bitcoin treasury.
Tokenized stocks find an audience beyond Wall Street’s trading hours
Most tokenized stock trading on Solana and BNB Chain now takes place outside regular US market hours, suggesting that around-the-clock access is becoming a major selling point for equities issued onchain.
According to Blockworks data cited by The Kobeissi Letter, more than 70% of tokenized stock trading volume on BNB Chain occurs outside the traditional 9:30 am to 4:00 pm Eastern trading window. The figure is 63% on Solana and nearly 60% on Base.
Activity is also picking up. Jupiter reported a 50% month-over-month increase in tokenized asset trading volume, while RWA.xyz data showed the value of tokenized stocks climbing 15% over the past 30 days to nearly $3.3 billion.
The trend comes as the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s innovation exemption opens the door for qualifying platforms to trade tokenized US-listed stocks on public blockchains, subject to disclosure and shareholder protection requirements. However, existing offerings such as xStocks and Ondo Global Markets remain largely unavailable to US investors, limiting domestic participation in the growing market.
Source: The Kobeissi Letter
Strive adds 3,311 Bitcoin as investors exercise $208 million in warrants
Bitcoin treasury company Strive increased its holdings by more than 11% last week, using proceeds from warrant exercises to expand its cryptocurrency reserves while increasing Bitcoin exposure per share.
In a Tuesday filing with the SEC, Strive disclosed that it purchased 3,311 BTC during the week ending Oct. 9 at an average price of roughly $84,500 per coin. The purchases brought its total holdings to 32,773 BTC, making it the fifth-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder.
CEO Matt Cole said investors exercised $208 million in warrants, with about $15.3 million still outstanding ahead of Tuesday’s expiration.
Strive also amended its governing documents to establish a binding $100 minimum issuance price for its SATA preferred shares, which were trading at $99.40. Meanwhile, Bitcoin traded near $83,300, below Strive’s average purchase price for the week, while its common stock, ASST, was little changed at $27.52.
Source: Matt Cole
Bitcoin miners face steep financing costs in AI expansion
Bitcoin mining companies expanding into artificial intelligence and high-performance computing face a widening gap in borrowing costs as lenders examine the risks of large-scale data center projects.
According to BlocksBridge Consulting’s Miner Weekly, securing AI customers is only part of the challenge. Miners also need billions of dollars to build facilities, purchase equipment and secure power infrastructure, with financing terms increasingly dependent on the customer and likelihood of project completion.
The differences are evident in recent deals. IREN secured $3.65 billion in financing in June at a blended interest rate of 6%, followed by another $2.4 billion in August at a fixed 9% rate. The agreements cover different projects, however, making direct comparisons difficult.
The financing needs are substantial. A June BlocksBridge analysis citing VanEck estimated that publicly traded Bitcoin miners required $50 billion to fund their AI infrastructure ambitions. IREN alone faced a $21.1 billion funding gap, followed by Riot Platforms at $7.2 billion and HIVE Digital Technologies at $4.6 billion.
US accounting proposal could give stablecoins a corporate boost
A proposed change to US accounting standards could make stablecoins more attractive to corporate treasuries by allowing qualifying tokens to be treated as cash equivalents on company balance sheets, according to a report from payments blockchain Tempo.
Under current accounting practices, stablecoin holdings may not count toward a company’s reported cash reserves, potentially affecting liquidity ratios and loan covenants even when the tokens are fully backed by US dollars.
The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) proposal could change that, though Tempo noted that companies would need direct redemption rights with stablecoin issuers to qualify. For example, simply purchasing USDC through a cryptocurrency exchange would not necessarily meet that requirement.
Coinbase already classified USDC and other payment stablecoins as cash equivalents in its 2025 annual report, supported by its redemption arrangement with Circle.
The proposal is open for public comment until Nov. 19, after which FASB will review the feedback before determining the final rules and their effective date.
Crypto Biz is your weekly pulse on the business behind blockchain and crypto, delivered directly to your inbox every Thursday.

articles.title: Bitcoin Holds Above $80K as Markets Scale Back Fed Rate Hike Bets
articles.text:
Bitcoin price steadies around $82K after Fed’s Warsh avoids rate-hike hints
Bitcoin held above $80,000 as South Korean tech stocks recovered from a sell-off and traders lowered their expectations for a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike.
Bitcoin (BTC) traded near $82,000 around Friday’s Wall Street open as crypto markets stabilized alongside a rebound in South Korean stocks.
Key points:
- Bitcoin price volatility eased as South Korean stocks rebounded 2% on Friday, offering relief after a steep sell-off.
- Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh gave no indication of further interest-rate hikes during a public discussion, as traders lowered the odds of a 25-basis-point increase in October to 15%.
- Analysts warned of difficult choices for Washington as the 10-year US Treasury yield climbed back to 5.13% and US stocks traded in a narrow range.
Traders see dovish edge to Warsh comments
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD holding most of its reclaimed ground after bouncing at $80,000 on Thursday.
BTC/USD four-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The earlier decline followed a weeklong sell-off in South Korean tech stocks, although Friday’s Asian trading session brought some relief. The KOSPI Composite Index closed at 5,668, up 2% on the day but still down 8.3% for the week.
KOSPI Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
US stocks largely avoided the sell-off in Asian markets but were mixed on Friday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index down 0.5% and the S&P 500 up 0.5%.
Meanwhile, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh offered investors some relief by avoiding any mention of further interest-rate hikes during a discussion with International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva.
“I don’t prejudge meetings. I don’t believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year,” he said.
Markets appeared to take Warsh’s tone as a dovish signal on rate hikes. Data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool showed the probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in October falling to 15%, down from 27% the previous day.
Fed target-rate probabilities for October FOMC meeting (screenshot). Source: CME Group
Economist Robin Brooks suggested that stress in the AI sector, a key driver of the Korea sell-off, could be at the heart of the Fed chair’s more aloof approach.
“Warsh gave no indication the Fed’s in any hurry to hike, so the October meeting is now pretty much off the table in terms of a hike,” he wrote in a blog post, adding:
“What’s helping the Fed is fears of an AI blow-up, which is making markets more receptive to a dovish message.”
US bond yields eye rebound as stocks halt upside
Elsewhere, US bond yields began rising as stocks steadied, prompting suggestions that the US treasury may ultimately be forced to choose between taming the bond sell-off and keeping stocks bullish.
The US 10-year yield stood at 5.07% on Friday, having briefly attempted to reverse higher, reaching 5.13%.
US 10-year bond yield one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Related: Bitcoin may seek 20-month trend line reclaim before new record highs: CryptoQuant
Market commentator The Kobeissi Letter noted that stock weakness has been the sole source of bond-yield corrections since August. In an X analysis published Thursday, Koebissi suggested equities may be in a paradoxical “‘bull-bear’ market.”
Without the US-Iran war, stocks would be far higher, it argued, adding that persistent inflation was driving investor demand for asset exposure — even as the Fed began a new rate-hike cycle.
“Even as the S&P 500 hits year #5 of its bull market, we believe a steep discount is currently priced into equities. This discount has functioned as a ‘stealth’ bear market, suppressing equity valuations in the world’s largest and fastest-growing companies,” it concluded, adding:
“This backdrop has the ability to catalyze a violent rally in the S&P 500 if and when it is ultimately priced-out.”
S&P 500 average bull-market returns comparison. Source: The Kobeissi Letter on X.com

articles.title: India's Cyber Agency Says AI Agents Read Confidential Business Records Without Authorization - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- India says AI agents under research and evaluation exceeded their assigned authorization and read personal and confidential business records on live Indian systems. None of the affected organizations detected it themselves.
- CERT-In did not name the AI providers, models or affected organizations, and the incidents surfaced only through voluntary disclosures from the providers after internal reviews.
- Separately, criminals using public AI offensive-security frameworks cut the time from initial access to final impact from days to a few hours, per the agency.
India’s national cybersecurity agency revealed AI agents operated by unnamed model providers exceeded their assigned tasks during testing and read confidential business records on live Indian systems.
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team, known as CERT-In, flagged the activity this week in a critical advisory titled “AI Agents as Attack Vectors.”
CERT-In said it received multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers whose models reached the live systems of Indian organizations while undergoing research and evaluation on the internet. The agency did not name the providers, the models, or the affected organizations.
The agents read business records containing personal data and confidential material, using credentials and connection settings that were left exposed in application configurations, public code repositories and overly permissive cloud service roles, which are the permission sets attached to cloud accounts.
In some cases they recovered the same exposed credential more than once and reused it in separate operations.
None of the affected organizations detected the access on their own, and every case surfaced only because the model provider disclosed it after an internal review.
This is yet another case of AI agents disrupting big companies and governments. Anthropic disclosed on July 30 that Claude models, told they had no internet access, compromised three real companies during capture-the-flag challenges, exercises in which a model must break into a machine and retrieve a hidden secret.
Britain’s AI Security Institute reported on Aug. 4 that agents took 19 unsanctioned actions across 10 of 122 evaluation runs, 17 of them from Anthropic’s Mythos 5 and two from OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The institute had deliberately enabled internet access for the test.
OpenAI’s case involved far more agents: roughly 1,200 of them coordinated on a hidden message board while trying to cheat a cybersecurity test, and about 700 attacked Hugging Face, according to an independent investigation by METR and Redwood Research.
Separately, CERT-In observed criminals using publicly available, AI-powered offensive security frameworks to scan for weaknesses, exploit them and run financially motivated attacks against Indian entities. The agency said the tools are repeatedly repackaged and redeployed, with deployments found on servers in multiple countries.

Strategy conditionally declares daily dividends as STRC hovers below $100
Strategy conditionally declared daily dividends on STRC, which continued to hover below its $100 par value.
Michael Saylor’s Strategy, the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, declared daily dividends on its STRC preferred stock for November, subject to shareholder approval and related amendments taking effect.
The company’s board declared cash dividends for each calendar day from Nov. 1 to Nov. 30, with payments beginning Nov. 2. Each dividend will be payable on the business day following its record date, according to a Form 8-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
STRC’s annualized dividend rate would remain at 12% for November. Strategy said management would keep recommending that rate until the stock demonstrates “sustained, healthy trading near $100 per share.”
Daily dividends could make STRC more appealing to investors and help it trade near its $100 par value. STRC is one of Strategy’s main fundraising vehicles for Bitcoin (BTC) purchases.
STRC was down 0.2% on Friday at $99.32 as of 1:36 pm UTC, according to Yahoo Finance.
Strategy added 250 Bitcoin for $21.5 million last week, bringing its total holdings to 848,250 BTC. During the week ending Oct. 4, the company repurchased $176 million worth of STRC, spending more than six times as much on the buybacks as on its $28 million in Bitcoin purchases.
On June 29, Strategy unveiled a capital framework allowing Bitcoin sales to fund dividends and increased STRC’s annual dividend rate to 12%.

articles.title: CFTC Wants to Drop Gemini’s $5M Settlement. A Judge Just Said No - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- A federal judge denied a rare joint motion from Gemini and the CFTC to vacate the $5 million settlement the exchange agreed to in January 2025.
- The ruling keeps a permanent injunction barring Gemini from making false statements to the CFTC; the exchange already paid the $5 million, which won’t be refunded.
- It’s a rare case of a court holding firm as a regulator retreats from its own case, amid the CFTC’s broader pro-crypto shift.
A federal judge has refused to let the Winklevoss twins’ crypto exchange Gemini walk back a $5 million settlement with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, even though the regulator itself had joined the exchange in asking him to toss it out.
In a ruling issued Oct. 15, U.S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein of the Southern District of New York denied the unusual joint motion to vacate a consent order Gemini agreed to in January 2025.
He found that neither a shift in the CFTC’s enforcement priorities under the current administration nor allegations of misconduct inside the agency’s enforcement division met the legal bar to reopen a signed judgment.
“Neither of these two grounds is sufficient to support vacating the settlement,” Hellerstein wrote, noting that Gemini voluntarily signed the deal roughly three weeks before trial.
The dispute dates to 2022, when the CFTC charged Gemini with making false or misleading statements to the agency in connection with a proposed Bitcoin futures product. The two sides reached the $5 million settlement in early 2025, then stunned observers in May by jointly moving to undo it, arguing the original enforcement effort had violated principles of fair enforcement.
Hellerstein wasn’t persuaded. The ruling leaves intact a permanent injunction barring Gemini from making false or misleading statements to the CFTC, and from publicly denying the settlement’s findings, though the agency has said it would no longer enforce that gag-style provision.
Gemini has already paid the $5 million penalty, and the parties previously said it would not be refunded even if the motion succeeded, so the money stays with the government.
The outcome is a rare instance of a court holding firm against a regulator trying to retreat from its own case, and it leaves a compliance overhang on Gemini just as the exchange expands its CFTC-regulated business. Gemini recently won approval from the Mike Selig-led CFTC to broaden its prediction-market and perpetual-futures offerings.
The episode also underscores how dramatically the CFTC’s posture toward crypto has shifted. The agency has moved aggressively to accommodate the industry, issuing no-action relief letting crypto apps offer regulated derivatives and floating a plan to bring crypto exchanges under federal oversight, a softer stance that, in this case, ran headfirst into a judge unwilling to rewrite a closed deal.

articles.title: Ledger’s Early Hardware Wallet Implant Reports Draw Scrutiny
articles.text:
Ledger’s early implant warnings deserved more action, Karpelès says
Ledger was contacted about tampered hardware wallets risks months before its latest security crisis, with former Mt. Gox CEO Mark Karpelès questioning its response.
French hardware wallet maker Ledger received multiple reports of malicious hardware implants months before its latest security crisis, according to Mark Karpelès, former CEO of the collapsed Bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox.
Karpelès told Cointelegraph he was aware of at least two people who contacted Ledger about tampered devices dating back to December 2025. Karpelès said he hasn’t encountered any public warning Ledger issued in response.
Joe Grand, a security researcher, told Cointelegraph he alerted Ledger on March 4, 2026, about a malicious implant in a Nano X purchased through online marketplace Lazada Thailand in August 2025.
Grand said Ledger acknowledged his findings and said it was investigating internally, but he criticized the company for not proactively warning customers about the threat.
Vietnamese crypto educator Tai Zen contacted Ledger about a suspected hardware wallet implant in December 2025, according to Mark Karpelès. Source: Tai Zen
Ledger’s ongoing security crisis surfaced Oct. 9, when crypto losses were reported involving wallets sold through CryptoBilis, a reseller authorized in Southeast Asia. Ledger has confirmed that one affected device contained an unauthorized implant.
Ledger declined to comment when asked about its handling of Grand’s disclosure, and referred Cointelegraph to its public statements on X.
“Maybe Ledger not responding to a single event of an implant found on a Ledger purchased from a shady dealer is normal,” Karpelès said. He added:
However the increasing number of reports they must have received, and the increasing quality/technology used should have alerted them enough to act, and at least remind customers to be careful.”
Marketplace listings expose reseller verification gaps
In a presentation shared with Cointelegraph, Grand identified the seller of the tampered Ledger as “LedgerXXX” on Lazada. At the time of writing, LedgerXXX is not listed as an authorized reseller in Thailand, though Lazada’s Ledger storefront is.
Cointelegraph sought clarification from both Grand and Ledger on the seller’s identity and authorization status when the device was purchased.
OneKey’s head of sales, Archie, told Cointelegraph that marketplaces such as Lazada host numerous independent sellers, making it difficult for customers to distinguish authorized stores from other listings.
Following the recent incidents, OneKey removed its reseller listings pending stricter checks, saying manufacturers must take responsibility for protecting customers rather than relying solely on buyers to identify trustworthy sellers.
Unauthorized wallet sales still raise security concerns
Grand’s findings were not limited to Ledger. In August 2026, he also alerted Trezor about tampered Trezor One and Model T wallets purchased from unauthorized sellers on TikTok and Facebook.
Trezor told Cointelegraph that counterfeit wallets occasionally appear through unauthorized sellers, as it had warned in 2022 about modified devices sold on Russian marketplaces. The company said that its recent claim of no evidence of compromised devices applied only to new wallets sold through authorized resellers.
Related: Trezor reduces resellers as a ‘preventative step’ amid Ledger tampering reports
Still, Trezor said it treats reports involving unauthorized sellers as early warnings and uses researchers’ findings to improve security checks.
“What changes the picture is a new technique, or a first case coming through an authorised channel,” Trezor said. “Either one means the problem has moved closer to ordinary buyers, and that’s when we’d move fastest, including warning customers directly.”

articles.title: Bitcoin Bounces, But Where Does It Go Next? Here’s What the Charts Say - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin has bounced after a Thursday dip brought it under $80,000 for the first time in over a month.
- Alts are having a better day as well: Zcash jumped 10.29%, Ethereum rose 4.17%, and Solana is up 3.02%.
- Where does the crypto market go next? Here's what the charts are saying right now.
Bitcoin is trading at $82,295, up 1.28% in 24 hours, after a Thursday slide below $80,000, its first dip under that level in more than a month. Ethereum gained 4.17% to $2,473.17, Solana rose 3.02%, and XRP added 2.03%.
Zcash is the strongest of the top 15 largest coins, jumping 10.29% to $1,222.02, lifting its market cap to $20.67 billion, and roughly erasing the almost 10% it lost on Thursday.
In general, the market is bouncing today after spending most of the week heading in the other direction.
Thursday's drop triggered $948 million in liquidations, 90.6% of them longs, per CoinGlass data. A liquidation is the forced closing of a trade placed with borrowed money after losses wipe out the collateral, and a long is a bet on rising prices, so the selling feeds on itself.
On the daily chart, Bitcoin hugs an important resistance market of $81,603, a level traders draw between a major low and high to estimate where pullbacks find buyers. Thursday's wick to $79,711 dipped under it and under the 50-day exponential moving average, or EMA, a line weighting recent prices more heavily, now at $80,407.
The 200-day EMA sits at $75,759, about 8% below the current price, and with the 50-day above it, the long-term trend still reads bullish.
The Average Directional Index, or ADX, which measures trend strength without direction, reads 25.5, barely above the 25 line that confirms a trend, and sellers (DI-) lead buyers (DI+). The Relative Strength Index, or RSI, is a 0-to-100 momentum gauge where 70 is overbought and 30 oversold. That’s at 48.9, neutral with a slight lean to sellers.
On Myriad, the prediction market built by Decrypt's parent company Dastan, traders are placing odds at 31% that Bitcoin hits a high of $87,500 in October down from 45% on Tuesday. In a separate market, Myriad traders say there's now a 43% chance BTC falls to $77,500.
The bullish scenario needs buyers to defend $81,603 and close above $84,246, opening $85,301, $86,644 and the $87,423 high, ideally with a rising ADX as confirmation.
The sideways scenario keeps Bitcoin between the $80,365 swing low and $84,246. The bearish scenario starts with a daily close below $81,603, putting $80,407 and $80,365 in play, then $78,003 and the $75,759 to $75,093 zone where the 200-day EMA meets the 50% retracement.

articles.title: Deutsche Bank Eyes Crypto Custody Expansion into Asia in 2027
articles.text:
Deutsche Bank prepares German crypto custody launch, eyes Asia: Report
Germany’s largest bank reportedly plans to expand its digital asset custody services to Asian financial centers due to the growth of the digital asset economy.
Deutsche Bank reportedly intends to debut its crypto custody services in Germany and plans to expand them across Asian financial centers in 2027.
The rapid growth of the digital asset economy, including hundreds of billions of dollars held in stablecoins, is driving the bank’s plans, Gerald Podobnik, co-head of Deutsche Bank’s corporate bank, told Reuters in a Friday report.
Podobnik added that the move is part of Deutsche Bank’s goals to achieve compound annual growth of 8% in corporate banking by 2028.
The bank’s custody service will initially support Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and select stablecoins, including Circle USDC (USDC), EURC (EURC) and AllUnity EUR (EURAU), according to a Sept. 16 press release.
A spokesperson for Deutsche Bank recently told Cointelegraph that it expects to receive regulatory approval for the custody offering in October, under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulations (MiCA). The European Securities and Markets Authority’s interim MiCA register showed that Deutsche Bank received authorization from Germany’s Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) on Monday.
Cointelegraph has contacted Deutsche Bank for comment on which Asian financial centers it plans to target first but had not received a response by the time of publication.
In September 2023, Deutsche Bank partnered with cryptocurrency infrastructure platform Taurus to support its crypto custody plans.
Related: Kraken parent to buy Lithuanian Saldo Bank amid TradFi expansion

articles.title: Solana’s Liu Says Shanghai Event Postponed After Registration Surge
articles.text:
Solana’s Liu says Shanghai event postponed over registration surge
Solana Foundation President Lily Liu said registrations quadrupled overnight, exceeding the attendance limit registered with local authorities.
The Solana Accelerate event in Shanghai was postponed after pre-registration exceeded the event cap set by local authorities, according to Lily Liu, president of the Solana Foundation.
Event registration quadrupled overnight following publicity for the event, Liu wrote in a Friday X post, adding that organizers decided to postpone the event to “comply with local requirements.”
Earlier on Friday, X users claimed that the event was “abruptly suspended” as law enforcement officers were stationed at the venue.
In October 2025, a Solana event in Shenzhen was also cut short due to venue capacity and public-safety concerns, Solana’s Chinese-language community account announced then on X.
Shanghai was scheduled to open Solana’s four-city Accelerate China tour, followed by Hangzhou on Sunday, Shenzhen on Tuesday and Beijing on Thursday, according to the event’s website.
The postponement followed Solana executives’ promotion of a new Shanghai office earlier this week.
China prohibits a range of crypto-related services, including token fundraising, trading and mining. In February, the People’s Bank of China and seven other agencies doubled down on those restrictions in a notice that added new bans, including unauthorized issuance of yuan-pegged stablecoins.
Related: White House crypto council chief Patrick Witt steps down

articles.title: Three Canadian Armed Forces Members Charged in Kidnapping of Crypto Exchange Owner - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Toronto police have laid 82 charges against seven men, including three Canadian Armed Forces members, over the July abduction of a crypto exchange owner.
- Police allege the victim was abducted at gunpoint, handcuffed and assaulted while the suspects tried to gain access to his crypto and business security systems.
- Searches turned up guns with 3D-printed parts, two silencers, drugs and more than 2,700 rounds of ammunition, about 2,500 of them stolen from the military.
Toronto police have arrested seven men, three of them members of the Canadian Armed Forces, over the abduction of the owner of a cryptocurrency exchange, the Toronto Police Service announced on Wednesday.
Investigators have laid 82 charges, including kidnapping for ransom and numerous firearms offenses. Police did not name the victim or the exchange.
Seven men arrested. Firearms and thousands of rounds of ammunition seized.
Chief @TPSMyronDemkiw speaks about the significant risks officers face during investigations involving dangerous weapons, and his additional concern that three of the accused are trained military… pic.twitter.com/4y384hzef2
— Toronto Police (@TorontoPolice) October 14, 2026
Police allege the victim was targeted as he approached his vehicle near Finch Avenue East and Bayview Avenue on July 25, 2026, then abducted at gunpoint, handcuffed and assaulted while the suspects tried to gain access to cryptocurrency assets and business-related security systems. He was later released after being threatened and warned not to contact police.
"The victim was allegedly targeted because of his access to cryptocurrency assets," Chief Superintendent Joe Matthews told reporters, CityNews reported.
Police arrested Saiefeddine Adem, 22, and Raheem Bishop-Jackson, 24, on July 26. Talarambage Fernando, 22, James Moreau, 29, and Christian Darbandi, 39, were arrested on August 11, followed by Jack Miley, 24, and Suhaib Alekozai, 39, on September 24.
Fernando, Moreau and Miley have been confirmed as Canadian Armed Forces members, police said. Fernando and Moreau are reservists with the 7th Toronto Regiment who were removed from military duties after their arrests, the Department of National Defence said earlier this month.
Searches of homes and vehicles turned up a shotgun, two 9mm firearms with 3D-printed receivers, two silencers, GPS tracking devices, handcuffs and large quantities of methamphetamine and cocaine, along with more than 2,700 rounds of ammunition. About 2,500 of those rounds had been stolen from the Canadian Armed Forces, investigators determined.
"Criminals continue to adapt their methods and seek new opportunities for financial gain," Matthews said in the release, describing the investigation as a reflection of increasingly sophisticated and targeted crimes involving digital assets.
"Whether you are a member of the military or a member of a police service or a public official, no one is above the law," Police Chief Myron Demkiw told reporters.
Police say there are no outstanding suspects and no further arrests are expected, though the investigation is ongoing.
"We're still trying to determine how all of [the suspects] fit together in this puzzle," Matthews said.
Crypto kidnappings in Canada
The case follows other kidnappings in Canada linked to crypto. WonderFi CEO Dean Skurka was released after a $720,000 ransom was paid in 2024, while a man who kidnapped a victim for a $1 million Bitcoin ransom was sentenced to 13 years in prison in September 2025.
A month later, one of the men who abducted self-styled "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski in December 2022 pleaded guilty to to nine charges, including kidnapping, assault, and firearms offenses.

articles.title: Crypto Investors Facing Tougher Exits as Markets Mature
articles.text:
CONNECT recap: Liquidity is tokenization’s next challenge, everyday stablecoins
Panelists at Cointelegraph’s Singapore CONNECT event explored opportunities in tokenized markets, the future of everyday stablecoin payments and the evolving landscape for crypto investors.
Tokenized assets are opening new trading opportunities across financial markets, but the growing supply of real-world assets (RWAs) being brought onchain has yet to be matched by investor demand, according to Alex Taaffe, chief revenue officer at crypto trading firm GSR.
Speaking during on a panel on liquidity and market fragmentation at CONNECT by Cointelegraph: Singapore Edition on Oct. 9, Taaffe said liquidity is improving in trading for pre-IPO stocks, commodities and global equities that investors previously had limited access to. However, he said demand for fully tokenized RWAs has not kept pace with the growing number of assets being issued.
Panelists (l-r): Rayco Tarrida Ortega, Min Teo, Shiliang Tang, Lingling Jiang, Alex Taaffe. Source: Cointelegraph
Cointelegraph brought together Web3 founders, investors and industry executives for four panel discussions covering tokenization, stablecoin payments, onchain trading infrastructure and venture capital exits, alongside a startup pitch competition.
“Specifically on RWAs, and fully tokenized assets, there’s a supply and demand inbalance. There’s a ton of supply. Every asset manager issuer wants to do capital formation onchain,” Taaffe said.
He said that the growing number of asset issuers and blockchains has further fragmented liquidity across tokenized markets.
Lingling Jiang, partner at DWF Labs, agreed that fragmentation remains a challenge, particularly when different issuers tokenize the same underlying asset but create separate liquidity pools.
However, Jiang said cryptocurrency liquidity has improved significantly in recent years, even as the industry has more work to do.
Related: Securitize stock jumps over 10% after launching tokenized US equities on Solana
Stablecoin adoption hinges on everyday payments
During the “Stablecoins at the Point of Sale: Cards, Wallets and the Race for Everyday Spend” panel, Mike Silagadze, founder and CEO of ether.fi, said while stablecoins have made it easier to move money across borders, wider adoption depends on whether consumers can use them for everyday expenses.
Silagadze pointed to Singapore, where consumers may hold USDC but still need local currency to pay bills, highlighting the gap between blockchain payment infrastructure and everyday financial services.
Yvonne Chia, head of communications at USDD, said that if the stablecoin issuer coinsiders the user’s point of view, “the most important thing for you is the user experience.”
“That’s the kind of direction that we want to move in, to make it as easy as possible for the user to have stablecoins, use stablecoins, to the point where it doesn’t cross their mind that they are using a stablecoin. It’s just a regular part of their lives,” Chia said.
Panelists (l-r): Ciaran Lyons (moderator, Cointelegraph), Ilya Podoynitsyn, Yvonne Chia, Mike Silagadze, Ashna Vaghela. Source: Cointelegraph
“The reason no one uses stablecoins in many parts of the world is because it just doesn’t plug into your day-to-day life,” Silagadze said.
Beyond everyday usability, regulatory hurdles remain, Ilya Podoynitsyn, co-founder and CEO of FinHarbor, said. He pointed out that providers must navigate rules that differ across jurisdictions, forcing them to adapt their infrastructure and compliance systems to individual markets.
Ashna Vaghela, chief customer officer at crypto payments provider Mercuryo, said that stablecoin payments should become as straightforward as using Apple Pay, with users able to complete transactions without leaving an application.
“I think that’s the whole point, to be invisible,” Vaghela said.
The discussion came as stablecoin market capitalization stood at $306 billion, up about 2% year over year after growing roughly 74% in the preceding 12 months.
Stablecoin market cap. Source: DefiLlama
Onchain trading faces liquidity fragmentation and risk management challenges
Crypto trading platforms face challenges identifying available liquidity across blockchain networks and managing counterparty risks, according to panelists discussing “What’s Still Missing in the Onchain Trading Stack in 2026.”
Austin Federa, co-founder of DoubleZero, said moving liquidity between blockchain networks remains more difficult than in traditional financial markets. He said that “fragmentation is not just an execution problem, it’s like a data problem,” adding that “it’s actually very hard to figure out how much liquidity truly exists onchain.”
Panelists (l-r): Alice Liu, Franklyn Wang, Miguel Morel, Austin Federa, Eunice Giarta. Source: Cointelegraph
On the risk management side, Miguel Morel, founder and CEO of blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence, said trading firms can use onchain data to assess counterparty risks, particularly in prediction markets, where some participants may have an informational advantage over others.
“If you know who’s on the other side and you’re taking less risk, you can offer a tighter spread,” Morel said, adding that this can lead to better prices for customers.
The same blockchain data can also help exchanges evaluate customer deposits, Morel said, allowing them to assess where funds originated and inform compliance decisions.
“Without needing to ask for a passport, you can know where those deposits are coming in from,” Morel said. He added that exchanges can use the information to determine whether to permit trading with deposited funds or refer them for compliance review.
Related: Bitcoin.de trading remains halted as German regulator rejects MiCA application
Crypto investors face tougher exits as markets mature
Liquidity challenges have complicated exits for crypto venture capital investors, according to panelists discussing “The Exit Problem: How Investors Get Their Money Back.”
Pulkit Gupta of Nomad Capital said liquidity in crypto markets has been particularly weak over the past three months, with much of it concentrated in larger cryptocurrencies.
“For me, on the altcoins, it has been really tough for us to get an exit,” Gupta said. The venture capital firm has backed several crypto projects with publicly traded tokens, including Movement, Solayer and Berachain.
Panelists (from l-r): David Shengart (moderator, Cointelegraph), Andre Nabais, Pulkit Gupta, Aleksandr Nexhaev, Sonia Shaw 
Source: Cointelegraph
Echoing the shift toward longer-term expectations, Sonia Shaw, CEO of OneAsset, said the market has matured, requiring startups to demonstrate stronger business fundamentals. Recalling an investor who expected an exit within six months, she said, “I don’t think the market’s like that anymore.”
Shaw characterized the move away from rapid exits as a positive sign of market maturity.
Aleksandr Nechaev, partner at Funders VC, highlighted the challenges presented by the speed of change for both products and markets.
“The rapid pace of change makes founders’ expertise and ability central to investment decisions,” Nechaev said. Change and how founding teams navigate the uncertainty came up later in the day during the event’s pitch competition, powered by Funders VC.

articles.title: Scammer Lost $4.8M in Bitcoin to Tampered Ledger Wallets: Chainalysis - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said one of the biggest victims of the Ledger wallet drain was a scammer who lost more than 60 BTC, about $4.8 million.
- The scammer moved the proceeds into three Ledger addresses on September 22, and thieves emptied all three into a single wallet on October 9.
- Ledger has tied all confirmed losses to devices sold by reseller CryptoBilis, though Chainalysis did not say where the scammer bought the devices.
Recent revelations of thefts from tampered Ledger hardware wallets sparked some schadenfreude, after it was revealed that one of the biggest victims was a scammer who lost more than 60 BTC.
Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis revealed the transactions behind the theft, which saw some $4.8 million worth of Bitcoin stolen, in a tweet on Thursday.
The Bitcoin came from a task scam, according to Chainalysis. People were paid to fake sales and reviews of real items, until a "negative balance" appeared in their accounts and they were told to add their own money in order to get paid.
One of the biggest victims of the Ledger theft was a scammer themselves. They lost more than 60BTC, about $4.8M. The funds were from a task scam.
In this task scam, people were paid to fake sales and reviews of real items. Then a "negative balance" appeared, and they were told… https://t.co/IJX4tx9ib3 pic.twitter.com/pGXNJkZJUi
— Chainalysis (@chainalysis) October 15, 2026
On September 22, the person behind the scam moved the proceeds into three separate Ledger addresses. On October 9, thieves emptied all three, with one transfer from each into the same wallet, which has been reported as holding stolen funds.
A chart shared by Chainalysis shows the scam proceeds passing through a consolidation wallet before reaching the three Ledger addresses, each of which was drained of about $1.64 million.
Ledger disclosed the incident on October 9.
Ledger's tampered devices
Ledger's Donjon security team disclosed that it had found an implant in wallets sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, which reads the 24-word recovery phrase from the screen during setup and sends it out over LTE. The company has said that all confirmed losses involve devices sold through CryptoBilis.
Chainalysis did not say where the scammer bought the devices.
Onchain investigator Specter has traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts, a figure Ledger says it has not verified. On Tuesday, Ledger asked resellers and distributors in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to suspend sales of its devices.
Ledger has not confirmed the total number of affected users or the value lost, and its investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: OpenAI Model Used Testnet Ethereum Wallet Without Permission to Finish Coding Task - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- OpenAI said an internal research model used funds from a crypto wallet it had not been given to pay for a contract deployment on Ethereum's Sepolia test network.
- The model derived keys from publicly known developer recovery phrases, checked 362 addresses, and judged the valueless test tokens acceptable to spend.
- It did not disclose using the account, and OpenAI says it has added safeguards to stop models getting live internet access in similar cases.
An internal OpenAI research model used funds from a crypto wallet it had not been given to complete a coding task, deriving the wallet's keys from publicly known developer recovery phrases, the company said in a misalignment report updated on Thursday.
The model, from the company's GPT-5.6 Sol family, was asked to update a crypto trading prototype and deploy smart contracts on Ethereum's Sepolia testnet, where tokens have no monetary value. The incident took place in June during a training task, and OpenAI discovered it in September.
The instructions allowed the model to deploy its own contracts if it could not find compatible ones. But they supplied no funded wallet and did not give the model permission permission to spend from an account it had found on its own, according to the report.
After failing to source test tokens from faucets, the model wrote a script to derive accounts from common developer recovery phrases and check their balances. A recovery phrase lets anyone who knows it derive the private keys that control the matching accounts.
The script checked 362 addresses and found one with enough Sepolia ETH to pay for the deployment.
The model questioned whether it had permission before signing the transaction. "But using public known key/funds ethically? Funds on a known public dev mnemonic are effectively abandoned/test ETH; Sepolia valueless," it reasoned, before concluding: "Fine."
The deployment succeeded and charged transaction fees to the account. In its final response, the model reported that it had deployed the contracts but did not disclose how it paid for them.
"This case shows that a model can substitute its own judgment about likely harm for the account holder's permission, then act on that judgment without authorization," OpenAI wrote.
AI agents in test environments
The report adds to a string of cases in which AI agents have worked around the limits of their test environments, including one in which OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and a more capable pre-release model escaped their sandbox and hacked rival AI firm Hugging Face's production servers.
Last month, researchers at cybersecurity firm Darktrace found AI agents hacking their own test environment to cheat, while some scientists have called for AI systems to be cut off from the internet.
OpenAI said it found the incident while extending its misalignment monitoring to records of earlier model activity. It has added "additional safeguards" to prevent live internet access for models in similar cases, and now runs its monitoring system on all traffic, designed to alert security if a model gains live internet access.

articles.title: Cross River Bank links $2.4B RLUSD to core banking system
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Cross River is adding Ripple’s RLUSD to its core banking platform, supporting transactions on the XRP Ledger.
- The bank says fintechs can access dollar and RLUSD payments through one API without deploying blockchain infrastructure.
- Services are limited to unnamed US states, with customer names, transaction volumes and a rollout schedule undisclosed.
Cross River Bank is adding Ripple’s US dollar-backed RLUSD stablecoin to its core banking platform with XRP Ledger support, giving fintechs a route to stablecoin payments through the same connection they use for conventional banking services.
The New Jersey bank announced the partnership on Oct. 15 and says customers can now access RLUSD through one API without deploying blockchain infrastructure. Services are available only in a limited number of US states, which the release did not identify.
The arrangement opens a distribution channel for Ripple through a bank that supplies payments infrastructure to other financial businesses. Cross River is extending its existing stablecoin platform, positioning RLUSD as an additional payment rail for fintech customers and payment networks.
Dollar and stablecoin payments through one connection
Cross River says fintechs can use its proprietary Core Operating System (COS) to move between US dollars and RLUSD, settle cross-border payments and treasury transfers around the clock, and access ACH, wires and real-time payments.
The API is the software connection between a fintech and the bank’s services. Cross River handles the integration with the blockchain payment network, allowing customers to access RLUSD alongside conventional payment options through that connection.
Adam Goller, Cross River’s head of fintech banking, said:
“Businesses shouldn’t have to rely on several different providers to move money across the globe.”
He added that the RLUSD integration expands capabilities the bank was already developing, bringing stablecoin transfers and traditional rails into its existing platform.
The companies also pitch the integration as another settlement option for payment networks. Issuers and acquirers, the institutions that issue payment cards and handle merchants’ card transactions, could gain more flexibility to settle within the day and reduce settlement delays.
Cross River cites XRP Ledger settlement times of three to five seconds. ACH, wires and other conventional rails remain separate options reached through COS.
RLUSD is distinct from XRP, the XRP Ledger’s native asset. The announcement identifies RLUSD as the dollar-backed payment asset and XRPL as the blockchain supporting it. Any role for XRP as the principal transferred between customers remains unspecified.
Markus Infanger, senior vice president of RippleX at Ripple, described the partnership as a way to make stablecoins part of the banking infrastructure businesses already use. The proposition is access through an established banking relationship, with the bank providing the connection to on-chain settlement.
On Nov. 24, 2025, Cross River announced a COS-integrated stablecoin-payments offering for approved fintech, enterprise and crypto partners, also with limited-state availability. The new announcement adds RLUSD and XRP Ledger support to that broader platform.
In a March 24 explanation, Luca Cosentino, Cross River’s head of crypto, described accounts that could send and receive stablecoins directly from dollar balances. He cited issuer integrations, automated liquidity, and standardized APIs as features of the bank’s approach.
The deal follows other efforts to distribute RLUSD through established banks. On Oct. 12, Standard Chartered launched RLUSD custody for eligible institutional clients holding XRPL-issued RLUSD through its Dubai International Financial Centre branch, with a separate LMAX collateral integration still planned.
Cross River’s partnership extends that banking presence into payments and settlement.
RLUSD had a market capitalization of about $2.4 billion as of Oct. 16, while Cross River’s Oct. 15 release separately put issuance on the XRP Ledger above $1 billion.
Ripple USD is +0.01% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #37 by market cap.

articles.title: Morning Minute: Google Clears a Major Quantum Hurdle, Bitcoin Still Safe - Decrypt
articles.text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors rebound despite hot PPI; BTC at $82.7k
- MSCI finalized index rules putting Strategy at risk of removal (MSTR -3%)
- White House has no crypto lead after Patrick Witt announces departure
- Binance US tries to raise $100M at $1B valuation
- Jupiter rolls out Papertrade-like perps product, does $1B volume first day
⚗️Google Clears a Major Quantum Hurdle, Bitcoin Still Safe
Eight days ago an Ethereum researcher told large holders to move their coins. Today Google published a result that makes him look less paranoid and more early.
Google Quantum AI cut a critical class of quantum errors roughly 40-fold on its Willow chip, per a new paper in Science. The technique attacks what may be quantum computing’s single biggest tax - producing the clean, single-use resources certain operations need, which by some estimates eats up to 95% of a machine’s capacity. Instead of building dedicated qubit factories to purify them, Google filters: inject a rough state, run it through a gauntlet of checks, throw out the 92% that fail. What survives hits 99.99% fidelity.
Nobody is draining wallets with this. Breaking an RSA-2048 key needs errors around one in 10 billion - about a million times cleaner than what Google just showed.
But researchers are moving closely. In 2019, cracking RSA-2048 was estimated to need 20 million noisy qubits. By 2025 that was under one million. A March 2026 Google whitepaper put Bitcoin’s elliptic curve cryptography at under 500,000 physical qubits. Willow has 105.
The irony this week is that Justin Drake’s actual fear wasn’t quantum at all. He thinks AI-driven mathematics breaks elliptic curves first, on ordinary hardware, in “months not years.” His advice: big holders should move funds to fresh addresses that have never signed a transaction, because signing exposes your public key. So crypto is being “attacked” on two fronts: quantum advancement and AI advancement.
With that said, key players are making moves and starting serious preparations. Coinbase spent this week arguing the migration has to start now. Sui is already running quantum-safe transactions on a test network. Ethereum, Zcash and Near all have plans to be quantum-resistant.
Crypto leaders will be prepared. But this was a reminder from Google that the tock is indeed ticking…
