articles.title: Bitcoin’s 20-Month Moving Average Stands Between Bulls And All-Time Highs
articles.text:
Bitcoin may seek 20-month trend line reclaim before new record highs: CryptoQuant
Bitcoin’s market cycle signals tool showed BTC price action copying history, possibly preparing to reclaim a key moving average before testing new highs.
Bitcoin is attempting to break through an “inflection frontier” that has historically triggered runs to new macro highs.
Key points:
- Bitcoin (BTC) may continue to new all-time highs if it successfully breaks through its 20-month moving average at $87,165, CryptoQuant reported.
- The market cycle signals metric showed BTC/USD poised to reclaim this “inflection frontier,” which it lost in December 2025.
- CryptoQuant’s bull-bear market cycle indicator continued to show Bitcoin as being in a bull market.
Analysis: Bitcoin “reset” complete as key trend line reappears
Data from onchain analytics platform CryptoQuant reveals that BTC/USD has begun a fresh battle with its 20-month simple moving average (SMA).
The 20-month SMA, at $87,165 as of Oct. 16, is the trend line around which the popular Bollinger Bands metric is constructed. This in turn forms the basis for CryptoQuant’s market cycle signals tool, which seeks to pinpoint Bitcoin’s position within its market cycle.
Bollinger Bands uses standard deviation to add an upper and lower band around the 20-month SMA. Currently, these sit at $121,640 and $52,694, respectively. CryptoQuant’s indicator describes the zone between the lower band and SMA as an “accumulation base,” while the SMA itself is referred to as an “inflection frontier,” a previous point of investor capitulation as price broke below it from above, most recently in December 2025.
BTC/USD one-month chart with Bollinger Bands. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
With Bitcoin now preparing to challenge the capitulation zone from below, history shows that successful breakouts have led to new cycle highs.
“Just over a year after the all-time high (ATH) of $124,709 on October 6, 2025, the market has concluded its ‘reset,’” CryptoQuant contributor GugaOnChain summarized in a blog post.
While Bollinger Bands are not intended to offer buy and sell signals, market cycle signals sees “smart money” taking profit once BTC/USD reaches its upper band. While this currently sits just below Bitcoin’s most recent all-time high of $126,200 from October 2025, CryptoQuant sees the next rally continuing beyond that level.
“While retail fears the current $82,442, thinking it’s the ‘top,’ the on-chain indicator BTC: Market Cycle Signals reveals that we are just warming up,” GugaOnChain added, referring to a current BTC price support zone.
Bitcoin market cycle signals chart. Source: CryptoQuant
The 20-month SMA has confluence with Bitcoin’s 2026 opening level at $87,490, boosting its strength as resistance. As Cointelegraph reported, large walls of ask liquidity remain in the vicinity across exchange order books.
Onchain data shows entrenching Bitcoin bull market
CryptoQuant maintains a broadly optimistic stance on Bitcoin’s emerging bull market despite crypto and risk assets navigating macroeconomic headwinds.
Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today
This week, contributor XWIN Research Japan flagged data from three onchain metrics that they said gave reason for “cautious optimism” for bullish momentum to return through the end of October.
In late August, CEO Ki Young Ju officially stated that the bear market was “over” based on readings from the bull-bear market cycle indicator. This uses composite data from several onchain profitability metrics, and shows bullish momentum accelerating with a reading of 0.186 on its scale versus 0.042 in August.
Bitcoin bull-bear market cycle Indicator. Source: CryptoQuant

articles.title: Cardano governance hits a wall as treasury reaches 91% cap
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Thirty enacted withdrawals have used 457.4 million ADA of Cardano's current 500 million allowance, leaving 42.6 million.
- Treasury inflows and returned grants increase assets but do not replenish the current gross withdrawal allowance.
- An unenacted 22 million ADA copper request would leave 20.6 million if enacted first under an unchanged limit.
Cardano has 42.6 million ADA left under its current treasury withdrawal allowance, even though the treasury itself holds about 1.38 billion ADA. New treasury withdrawals must fit inside that remaining authority or follow a newly agreed limit.
As of Oct. 16, 2026, 30 enacted treasury-withdrawal actions from epoch 613 totaled 457,395,629 ADA. Against the agreed 500 million ADA ceiling, that leaves about 8.5% of the allowance for the period ending around July 3, 2027.
A new 22 million ADA copper-reserve request would consume more than half that room if enacted. For developers seeking another grant and ADA holders deciding how to allocate public funds, the choice depends on how much additional funding governance can approve. Programs funded by earlier withdrawals can continue paying for work from money already allocated.
How Cardano's withdrawal allowance works
Cardano's Net Change Limit agreement covers epochs 613 through 713, beginning Feb. 13, 2026, and ending around July 3, 2027. It counts withdrawals already debited during that period, including those made before the limit increased.
Despite its name, this agreement measures gross withdrawals. Reserve allocations, transaction-fee income, donations, and returned grant money do not offset the amount counted against the ceiling. Expected, draft or unratified withdrawals also do not count: the relevant event is an enacted action debiting the treasury.
| Current allowance accounting | ADA | 
|---|---|
| Agreed withdrawal ceiling | 500,000,000 | 
| Enacted withdrawals since epoch 613 | 457,395,629 | 
| Remaining withdrawal authority | 42,604,371 | 
The latest Koios balance available at retrieval was about 1.378 billion ADA in epoch 661, up from about 1.337 billion ADA in epoch 650. That is an increase of about 40.9 million ADA, while the withdrawal allowance remains unchanged.
Incoming ADA can strengthen the treasury's assets without expanding the amount authorized to leave it. Returning unused funding similarly benefits the treasury balance but does not erase the original withdrawal from this period's accounting.
An InfoAction submitted July 2 recorded the 500 million ADA limit. Its final voting summary, from epoch 647, shows 62.35% stake-weighted DRep support. Delegated representatives (DReps) exercise voting power assigned by ADA holders.
The Cardano Constitution requires agreement of more than 50% of active voting stake for an NCL and prohibits withdrawals that exceed the applicable limit. The Constitutional Committee reviews whether governance actions comply with the charter, while individual treasury withdrawals require their own approvals.
An InfoAction records agreement without itself withdrawing funds or enacting a protocol parameter. Cardano Foundation's Aug. 5 meeting notes recognized the increase to 500 million ADA. That agreement remained the latest NCL in the InfoAction records checked on Oct. 16.
The constitutional limit applies to additional withdrawals. Money already withdrawn remains available under its program's delivery and oversight arrangements, and governance can agree another limit.
What the remaining authority means for funding
The Cardano Strategic Copper Reserve request seeks 22 million ADA. Proposed in epoch 661, it remained unratified and unenacted in the Oct. 16 snapshot, so it has not reduced the remaining allowance.
If it were enacted in full before any other new withdrawal, with the limit unchanged, headroom would fall to 20,604,371 ADA. Under those assumptions, it fits within today's remaining authority, but approving it would leave less capacity for other requests.
Voters would be allocating more than half the current room to this single proposal.
The project commits to returning realized net copper-sale proceeds and unused funds by month 36, without guaranteeing recovery of the original ADA principal. Any eventual return would replenish treasury assets without reopening this gross-withdrawal allowance.
That creates a specific trade-off for DReps assessing the proposal. A potential future recovery of treasury assets does not preserve room for another withdrawal during this period. The immediate allowance cost would be the full 22 million ADA, irrespective of any later refund.
OpenZeppelin's separate 11,787,063 ADA stack request expired in epoch 661 without ratification or enactment. This withdrawal did not fund the project, and its proposed 12-month quarterly delivery schedule did not consume the ceiling. An unsuccessful request leaves the allowance available for other decisions.
The latest enacted withdrawal in the period was 120 million ADA for AlphaGrowth's Cardano PRIME in epoch 650, beginning Aug. 17. That debit is already included in the 457.4 million ADA cumulative total.
PRIME's funded terms describe a 12-month program administered by Intersect, with phased releases, a Month 4 gate for Phase 3, and return triggers for unused, unearned, or unreleased funds. The treasury withdrawal and later releases to the program are separate steps.
In its Oct. 9 update, funding administrator Intersect reported that MLabs' Plutarch and Ply maintenance contract had been funded that week for 12 months of work across four quarterly cycles.
Its Oct. 2 report also described withdrawn budgets held in live contracts. Such arrangements let funding already outside the treasury support work in subsequent months.
As the team approaches its next milestone, the practical question is whether payment comes from an existing allocation or requires a new treasury withdrawal.
Only a new withdrawal uses additional room under the allowance. The remaining 42.6 million ADA does not reflect recipients' cash balances or the value of work they still need to deliver.
DReps can prioritize requests within that amount, consider smaller withdrawals or defer them until they fit an applicable limit, and they can also agree to another NCL.
Those governance decisions determine how much additional funding Cardano can authorize during the current period.
Cardano is -1.54% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #15 by market cap.

articles.title: Capital B Reports $78M H1 Loss Driven by Bitcoin Impairment Charge
articles.text:
Capital B reports $78M H1 loss driven by Bitcoin impairment charge
Europe’s second-largest Bitcoin treasury raised $30 million and increased its Bitcoin holdings by 11% in the first half of 2026, despite reporting a $75 million Bitcoin impairment loss.
France-listed Bitcoin treasury company Capital B reported a net loss of 69.5 million euro ($78 million) for the first half of 2026, driven by a Bitcoin impairment charge of $75.8 million.
The impairment reflected Bitcoin (BTC) prices as of June 30 and had no direct cash impact, according to the company’s first-half 2026 report, published Thursday.
Still, Capital B’s consolidated revenue rose 3.5% year-over-year to $6.5 million, while adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.2 million. EBITDA measures a company’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.
The results show that the European Bitcoin treasury firm continued raising funds to fuel its Bitcoin accumulation despite the accounting losses. Capital B announced capital raises totaling $30 million in the first half of the year and increased its Bitcoin holdings by 11%, from 2,823 BTC in January to 3,139 BTC by the end of June.
The company’s total holdings subsequently reached 3,538 Bitcoin by Sept. 30, marking a 25% increase from the beginning of the year. Capital B’s treasury is currently worth $290 million, ranking it as the world’s 25th-largest corporate Bitcoin treasury and Europe’s second-largest by holdings, following Germany-based Bitcoin Group, according to Bitcointreasuries.
Capital B’s stock price rose by 0.5% in early morning trading on Friday, but was down 25% year-to-date, according to Yahoo Finance.
In July, Capital B approved a 10-for-1 reverse stock split aimed at broadening its institutional investor base. In June, its shareholders approved up to $120 billion in financing capacity, including equity and credit instruments, to support the company’s Bitcoin accumulation strategy.
Related: Bitcoin will become ‘less volatile’ and larger than gold: ‘The Bitcoin Standard’ author

articles.title: USDC processed $36 trillion in H1 transactions, but Circle kept just 7 cents of every revenue dollar
articles.text:
Quick Take
- USDC captured a reported 77% of stablecoin transaction volume in June, yet Circle retained just seven cents in profit per revenue dollar.
- Coinbase held an average $20 billion in USDC, underscoring the growing influence of major distributors over stablecoin adoption and earnings.
- Circle now faces a critical test: Can it maintain USDC's market position while competitors offer partners more generous revenue-sharing deals?
Stablecoin issuer Circle spent 93% of its first-half revenue on distribution, operations, and investment as USDC processed more than $36 trillion in transactions.
The stablecoin issuer generated about $1.4 billion in revenue in the first six months of 2026, but $819 million went to distribution partners and transaction costs, while another $473 million covered operating expenses and network investment.
Circle retained roughly seven cents of every dollar earned as net profit, about $103 million.
The figures, released Oct. 16 by Chief Commercial Officer Kash Razzaghi, form part of Circle's response to newer stablecoin providers promising businesses a bigger share of the earnings generated by digital dollars.
Circle argues that the money it retains must pay for the banking access, liquidity, and compliance systems that let USDC operate across international markets.
Coinbase helps drive Circle's $819 million distribution bill
Circle earns most of its revenue from the assets backing USDC, which include cash and US government securities. Exchanges, wallets, and payment companies that attract users and maintain USDC balances receive a share of the income those balances generate.
That arrangement makes distribution a significant expense, but it also gives major partners a financial incentive to promote USDC. The more customers and balances a platform brings to the network, the more it can earn.
Coinbase remains Circle's largest and longest-standing distribution partner. Average USDC held across the exchange's products reached a record $20 billion in the second quarter, up 44% from a year earlier, according to figures Circle cited.
Circle has been extending that approach beyond its longstanding US partner. Binance signed a five-year commercial agreement in September and invested $100 million in Circle, while more than 150 other partners have an economic interest in USDC's growth.
Those agreements give Circle access to exchanges, fintech applications, banks and payment services that already serve millions of customers. They also make the issuer's share of retained revenue an increasingly important consideration as rival stablecoins compete for the same distribution channels.
USDC's $36 trillion transaction boom comes with liquidity costs
Circle said USDC processed more than $36 trillion in on-chain transaction volume in the first half of 2026. By June, it accounted for approximately 77% of global stablecoin transaction volume, up from 60% a year earlier, according to the company's figures.
The transaction activity reflects how extensively USDC moves across blockchain networks. Separately, Circle reported more than $315 billion in combined issuance and redemptions over the six months, about $1.7 billion daily.
Second-quarter minting and redemptions totaled $170 billion, up 105% from the same period last year, indicating growing demand for moving money between traditional banking accounts and blockchain-based dollars.
Supporting that activity requires substantial cash reserves and banking infrastructure, particularly as payment companies increasingly demand access to dollars outside normal business hours.
Circle says direct customers have always been able to redeem USDC without fees through regular banking channels, where settlement can take up to two business days.
The company now offers eligible customers free, near-real-time redemptions through the Circle Payments Network and its platform products, allowing participating businesses to convert USDC into dollars around the clock.
However, faster conversions come at a cost.
Circle holds cash at banking partners so customers can receive dollars when they redeem USDC, including during weekends and holidays. That money must remain readily available and typically earns less than funds invested in Treasury securities.
Maintaining those balances, along with the banking relationships needed to move them, ties up resources Circle could otherwise invest elsewhere.
Circle challenges rivals over stablecoin profit sharing
Razzaghi's statement directly challenged newer stablecoin providers that claim established issuers retain too much reserve income and charge excessive redemption fees.
Circle's position is that sharing more earnings with distributors must be balanced against the expense of maintaining the infrastructure required to support growing transaction activity.
The company pointed to more than 55 licenses and regulatory registrations, relationships with over 25 banking partners and native USDC deployments across more than 35 blockchains.
It also highlighted reserves held in a government money market fund managed by BlackRock and custodied at BNY, alongside compliance operations covering 185 countries.
These investments help Circle serve financial institutions operating under different regulatory requirements while maintaining the liquidity needed to process large withdrawals.
However, competing stablecoin issuers are increasingly offering payment platforms and other distributors greater participation in reserve earnings, creating pressure on the economics of Circle's existing arrangements.
The company now faces the commercial challenge of attracting additional USDC balances while preserving enough revenue to fund its expanding settlement network.
Circle is scheduled to report third-quarter financial results on Nov. 4, giving investors another chance to assess how distribution costs are changing as the issuer expands partnerships and offers faster, free redemptions to more businesses.

articles.title: Judge Rejects CFTC, Gemini Bid to Undo $5M Settlement
articles.text:
Judge rejects CFTC, Gemini bid to undo $5M settlement
Judge ruled changes in CFTC enforcement priorities and allegations of misconduct by its enforcement division were insufficient to overturn Gemini’s January 2025 settlement.
A US federal judge has rejected a joint request by crypto exchange Gemini and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to overturn a $5 million settlement, despite the regulator’s conclusion that it would not have pursued the case under current enforcement standards.
On Thursday, US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein ruled that changes in CFTC enforcement priorities and allegations of misconduct by its enforcement division did not justify overturning the January 2025 settlement.
On May 27, the CFTC and Gemini jointly asked the court to overturn the settlement after an internal agency review found alleged misconduct by the regulator’s enforcement division, including reliance on a questionable whistleblower, improper regulatory pressure and efforts to prevent the disclosure of evidence.
The ruling leaves intact a permanent injunction barring Gemini from making false or misleading statements to the CFTC. The settlement also prohibits Gemini from publicly denying its findings, although the regulator said in June that it would no longer enforce such restrictions.
Gemini has already paid the $5 million penalty, which the CFTC previously told Cointelegraph would not be refunded even if the settlement were overturned.
Judge cites Gemini’s decision to settle before trial
The case centered on how Gemini operated its Bitcoin auction. According to the January 2025 consent order, the exchange failed to disclose that some customers traded using borrowed funds, that self-trading had occurred despite safeguards and that certain traders received special fee arrangements.
Gemini also submitted trading volume data without disclosing that some of the activity involved these practices.
Related: Better Markets says CFTC is ‘wrong agency’ to regulate retail crypto
Hellerstein said Gemini was already aware of problems with the CFTC’s case when it agreed to settle, less than three weeks before trial. Although the exchange later obtained additional internal CFTC documents, the judge ruled that the new information was not enough to overturn a settlement Gemini had voluntarily accepted.
The judge also rejected the argument that President Donald Trump’s digital asset executive order and the regulator’s new enforcement approach warranted relief, saying they reflected changes in policy rather than a significant change in law.
Former CFTC Chair Timothy Massad previously called the regulator’s move to reverse a settled case “extraordinarily unusual,” telling Cointelegraph that the public “deserves a better explanation.”
Magazine: Can the SEC and CFTC’s pro-crypto rules be overturned? Legal opinion

articles.title: GTA 6 Trailer Features Meme Coin—And Solana Copycat Soars 2,900% - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- GTA 6's launch trailer was released on Thursday and briefly mentioned "Dacity Coin," which has caused an on-chain frenzy.
- A copycat Solana meme coin skyrocketed 2,900%, thanks to the trailer, with dozens of traders profiting more than $10,000 each.
- The token existed five days before the trailer release, after degens found mention of Dacity Coin in leaked GTA 6 footage.
Two seconds of the Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer was all it took for a Solana meme coin to fly, making some traders pretty rich.
Dacity Coin was seen plastered along the side of a plane in the GTA 6 launch trailer released on Thursday, with a man setting off a neon pink flare on the wing. This prompted a real meme coin of the same name to skyrocket 2,900% from a $104,000 market capitalization to $3.18 million, in the hour following the trailer's release.
Interestingly, the token had been created five days prior, after notorious Rockstar hacker "Cyberleek" leaked GTA 6 gameplay revealing that Dacity Coin was set to be in the game—but only a comparatively small group of traders noticed.
Upon its October 11 launch on Solana launchpad Pump.fun, Dacity Coin hit a peak market cap of $1.14 million before falling to $144,700 over the coming day and trading sideways until Thursday's sharp rise.
$Dacity coin confirmed in the game
This is the 100m runner we’ve been waiting for early not wrong on my pump call out
Check the 54 second mark https://t.co/LTv2BmRubD https://t.co/hCDN0NwVsF pic.twitter.com/DPwbdVK2Mg
— COREY (@Corey_Ape) October 15, 2026
As a result, traders had plenty of time to buy into the meme coin before it skyrocketed. According to DEX Screener, 24 traders profited more than $10,000 on the token, with the top trader turning $1,912 into $44,000.
Dacity now sits at a $1.5 million market cap, dropping around 53% from its $3.18 million peak.
What is Dacity?
In the launch trailer, the plane reads "DacityCoin AudaCity," and in previously leaked footage, the game's protagonist Lucia can be seen skydiving wearing an AudaCity parachute. When the parachute opens, per the leaked screenshots, it features the slogan "Quit your job. Sell your house. Move [ineligible]."
According to the GTA wiki, Lucia is asked to parachute as a stunt to advertise the AudaCity brand and attract investment to the Dacity Coin.
If true, the game appears to be satirizing the stunts that meme coin creators have performed to promote their tokens over the years. In 2024, Decrypt reported that a man set himself on fire to promote his meme coin while others smoked drugs on livestream, pretended to be a dog, or recklessly shot a pistol out of their window.
This falls on the backdrop of years-long rumours of cryptocurrencies featuring in GTA 6. Several theories were thrown out, including play-to-earn features, NFT-owned properties, and even an entire blockchain for the game. However, all of them were unsubstantiated—Dacity Coin is the first solid sign of cryptocurrency being in the upcoming game.
How prominent will Dacity Coin be in the upcoming GTA 6 game? That's the question currently on the lips of traders. If it's a mainstay of the game, then degens might stand to profit handsomely from holding the token for longer. If not, well, this might be the end of the road.
Déjà vu
This has all happened before.
In February 2025, Fortnite added a fake crypto coin called Dill Bits, and degens quickly launched a real one on Solana that hit a $4.78 million market cap before crashing 96%. It pumped 2,700% again in April after Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney called it a scam, then dropped 82% within days.
“I didn’t launch it. What is wrong with you people,” Sweeney posted, as traders floated theories that he was secretly behind the coin.
I didn’t launch it. What is wrong with you people.
— Tim Sweeney (@TimSweeneyEpic) April 6, 2025
The Dill Bits community took the whole thing as bullish, given that Fortnite’s storyline was literally about a pickle villain called Big Dill running a crypto rug pull. It didn’t help much, with DB dropping 82.3% in the days that followed.
Epic Games told Decrypt at the time that there was “no real cryptocurrency or memecoin associated with Fortnite or endorsed by Epic.”
Rockstar has yet to say anything about Dacity Coin, and the game studio did not respond to Decrypt's request for comment.

articles.title: OpenAI Model Spent Testnet ETH Without Authorization
articles.text:
OpenAI model helped itself to testnet crypto, then kept quiet about it
An OpenAI research model checked 362 wallet addresses, questioned whether using the funds was ethical and proceeded with a transaction it later omitted from its final task summary.
An internal research model at OpenAI accessed a funded crypto wallet without authorization, using testnet Ether to deploy smart contracts on the Sepolia network and later omitting the spending from its final task summary.
OpenAI said the model, which was part of its GPT-5.6 Sol family, was given the task of updating a crypto trading prototype and deploying compatible contracts. After failing to obtain testnet ETH through faucets, the model derived accounts from publicly known developer recovery phrases, checked 362 wallet addresses and selected one with enough funds to proceed.
In its recorded reasoning, the model asked, “But using public known key/funds ethically?” It then argued that the funds were “effectively abandoned/test ETH” and that Sepolia ETH had no value, before using the wallet’s private key to sign and broadcast a deployment transaction. The transaction succeeded, with fees charged to the account.
OpenAI said the incident showed how an AI model could decide on its own that using someone else’s funds was acceptable, even without permission. The company discovered the incident while reviewing earlier model activity and has since introduced safeguards to prevent live internet access in similar situations.
OpenAI incident adds to concerns over autonomous AI agents
The incident happened on June 26, but was not discovered until Sept. 25, nearly three months later, according to OpenAI. The transaction did not transfer ETH to another wallet but charged the account network fees for deploying a contract.
OpenAI said its misalignment monitoring system now runs across all traffic and is designed to alert security personnel if a model obtains live internet access.
Related: Anthropic warns ‘AI worms’ may autonomously spread across devices like a virus
The wallet incident follows other disclosures involving OpenAI models acting beyond their authorization or concealing their actions.
On Sept. 16, OpenAI disclosed six other cases of AI misalignment. In one case, instances of GPT-5.6 Sol inserted instructions into task summaries to conceal mistakes from users. Another case involved a model using an exposed API key without authorization before fabricating figures it could not retrieve.
OpenAI said those earlier disclosures were not intended to indicate how frequently misalignment occurs across its models.
Concerns about autonomous agents handling digital assets also predate the latest disclosure. In June, researchers warned that autonomous AI agents equipped with crypto wallets could cause unintended harm even when deployed for legitimate purposes. The researchers recommended safeguards, including emergency shutdown mechanisms, to limit potential risks.
Magazine: Scammer loses $4.8M stored on tampered Ledgers: Asia Express

articles.title: OpenAI's rogue crypto agent spent funds without permission, exposing risks to autonomous wallets
articles.text:
Quick Take
- OpenAI revealed that a research model accessed an Ethereum testnet wallet and spent its funds without permission after questioning the ethics of doing so.
- The incident exposes financial authorization risks as Coinbase and MetaMask expand AI wallets capable of executing crypto transactions autonomously.
- The SEC is weighing whether AI agents should authorize crypto transactions, raising questions about how firms can prevent unauthorized spending.
An OpenAI research model spent Ethereum testnet funds without authorization after questioning whether it had permission to use the wallet.
The company disclosed that an internal GPT-5.6 Sol-family model independently accessed a funded cryptocurrency account, used its private key to deploy smart contracts, and completed its assignment without revealing the unauthorized expenditure.
The incident, detailed in an Oct. 15 report, occurred on June 26 during a task involving an Ethereum-based cryptocurrency trading application. OpenAI discovered the activity on Sept. 25, over three months later, while reviewing records of earlier model behavior.
The disclosure comes as cryptocurrency companies expand financial services that allow AI agents to execute transactions independently, while US regulators consider whether software should be authorized to control digital assets.
According to OpenAI, the model was instructed to update a trading prototype and deploy compatible smart contracts on Ethereum's Sepolia test network. However, it received neither a funded wallet nor permission to spend assets from independently discovered accounts.
After unsuccessfully attempting to obtain test ETH through cryptocurrency faucets, the model developed a script that generated wallet addresses from publicly known developer recovery phrases.
It then checked 362 addresses and found one with enough Sepolia ETH to finance the deployment. The publicly available recovery phrase allowed it to derive the account's private key without compromising Ethereum's cryptographic security.
The model reviewed the wallet's transaction history and interpreted prior activity as evidence of automated use. It then explicitly questioned whether using the account's funds would be ethical.
However, it reasoned that the public recovery phrase and the negligible monetary value of Sepolia ETH made the assets effectively abandoned, allowing it to proceed with the transaction.
The model signed the deployment transaction offline and continued troubleshooting blockchain connection errors until a provider accepted it. Although the transaction transferred no ETH to another recipient, the account paid the network fees required to deploy the contract.
Subsequent checks verified code deployed to 10 addresses, and the project passed 12 unit tests and completed a production build.
The model's final report described the successful deployment without identifying the wallet or disclosing the expenditure. OpenAI's investigation highlighted how the system substituted its assessment of potential harm for the account holder's authorization.
SEC and crypto wallet providers confront AI spending risks
The incident raises questions about financial controls as companies increasingly give autonomous AI agents the ability to make cryptocurrency payments, execute trades, and manage decentralized finance positions.
The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is already examining that issue under a crypto custody proposal introduced Oct. 1.
The proposed framework would require registered investment advisers seeking to hold eligible client crypto assets themselves to implement safeguards, including transaction authorization by at least two designated people.
Crucially, Question 77 asks whether AI, smart contracts and other software agents should be permitted to act as transaction signatories, and whether their participation strengthens or weakens asset protection.
That question has become increasingly relevant as crypto companies develop infrastructure that lets AI systems control funds within predetermined limits.
In February, Coinbase introduced Agentic Wallets, enabling software agents to make payments, execute trades, and interact with DeFi protocols without requiring human approval for every transaction.
Its safeguards include transaction limits, session spending caps, risk screening, and isolated private keys that remain outside the AI model's direct access.
MetaMask followed in August with an Agent Wallet offering spending restrictions, approved protocol lists, and transaction screening. Its Guard Mode requires additional approval for activities exceeding user-defined permissions.
These controls restrict transactions processed through designated wallets, but the OpenAI incident illustrates another potential exposure: agents with access to external tools can independently discover credentials and use alternative routes to execute transactions.
The research model did not interact with Coinbase or MetaMask's agent-wallet infrastructure, and its behavior does not establish a weakness in either product. It nevertheless highlights the need to enforce financial permissions across an agent's broader operating environment.
The financial stakes would be considerably higher if similar behavior occurred on Ethereum's mainnet, where validly signed transactions can transfer assets with substantial monetary value and generally cannot be reversed.
For companies deploying AI trading or treasury agents, preventing unauthorized spending may require independent transaction approval, restrictions on credential access, and monitoring that reconciles on-chain activity with authorized instructions.
OpenAI said it has introduced additional safeguards to restrict live internet access in similar research environments and expanded monitoring designed to alert security personnel when that access occurs.
Meanwhile, the SEC is accepting comments on its proposed custody framework until Dec. 7, including whether automated signatories should be permitted under institutional custody requirements.
The responses could influence how regulated investment firms incorporate AI into cryptocurrency operations, particularly whether autonomous systems can authorize transactions independently or must remain subject to human-controlled approval mechanisms.

articles.title: What Is a Hardware Wallet? Crypto Cold Storage Explained - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Hardware wallets are physical devices that keep crypto private keys offline, signing transactions internally so the keys never touch an internet-connected device.
- They are not hack-proof: a Coldcard firmware bug and tampered Ledger devices sold through a reseller both led to major losses in 2026.
- Wallet manufacturers are looking to future-proof their devices for a future of agentic finance and quantum computing.
There's an old saying in crypto: "not your keys, not your coins." When you leave Bitcoin, Ethereum or any other cryptocurrency on an exchange, the exchange holds the private keys that control those funds. If it gets hacked, goes bust or freezes withdrawals, you may have no way to get them back.
The obvious fix is to hold your own keys, which is called self-custody. That brings its own problem, though. A private key stored in a software wallet on an internet-connected phone or laptop can be stolen by malware, phishing sites and remote attackers.
Hardware wallets were built to solve this. They're small physical devices that keep your private keys offline, so you can sign crypto transactions without your keys ever touching a device connected to the internet. In this guide we'll explain what hardware wallets are, how they work, who makes them, and where the technology is heading after an eventful 2026.
What is a hardware wallet?
A hardware wallet is a dedicated physical device, usually about the size of a USB stick or credit card, that generates and stores the private keys for your crypto. It's a form of "cold storage," because the keys stay offline. A "hot wallet" like a browser extension or mobile app is the opposite.
One common misconception is that your coins live on the device. They don't. Your crypto always lives on the blockchain. The hardware wallet holds the keys that prove you own it and let you move it.
The category dates back more than a decade. Trezor, made by Czech firm SatoshiLabs, calls itself the inventor of the hardware wallet in 2013. France-based Ledger was founded in 2014 and has since reported sales of more than eight million devices.
Did you know?
When you set up a hardware wallet, it gives you a "seed phrase" of 12 to 24 words. Anyone who has those words can recreate your wallet and take your funds, so never photograph them, type them into a website, or save them to cloud storage.
How does a hardware wallet work?
When you first switch on a hardware wallet, it uses a random number generator to create your private keys. A seed phrase backs them up, and a PIN code protects the device.
When you want to send crypto, you build the transaction in companion software on your computer or phone, such as Ledger Wallet (formerly Ledger Live), Trezor Suite or Sparrow. The software sends the unsigned transaction to the hardware wallet. You check the details on the device's own screen and confirm with a physical button or touchscreen. The device then signs the transaction inside its own hardware and sends back only the signature. The private key never leaves the device.
Devices connect in different ways, and each comes with security trade-offs:
- USB: the classic wired connection.
- Bluetooth and NFC: wireless options for mobile users.
- QR codes or microSD cards: "air-gapped" devices that never connect to another device directly.
Many devices also use a secure element, a tamper-resistant chip like the ones in passports and bank cards, to guard keys against physical attacks.
Did you know?
"Clear signing" means a wallet shows transaction details in plain language rather than raw code, so you know what you're approving. That matters because scammers often trick people into signing malicious smart contract approvals.
What's so special about hardware wallets?
Their main advantage is isolation. Even if your laptop is full of malware, an attacker can't take your keys out of a well-designed hardware wallet or approve a transaction without you physically confirming it.
Hardware wallets have improved over the years, evolving from miniscule screens and clunky interfaces to modern devices that incorporate Bluetooth, NFC and even touchscreens and cameras.
Hardware wallets are also starting to do more than just crypto storage. Ledger added stablecoin yield through Kiln in April 2025, Tangem followed with Aave later that year, and Trezor launched native stablecoin yield through Morpho vaults in May 2026.
Who makes hardware wallets?
- 🔐 Ledger combines its secure element chips and Donjon white hat hacking team with slick hardware design.
- 🛡️ Trezor is the open-source pioneer behind the Safe 3, Safe 5 and Safe 7.
- 📷 Keystone makes air-gapped wallets that sign transactions by QR code.
- 💳 Tangem makes NFC cards that tap against your phone and can skip seed phrases entirely.
- 🔑 Bitkey from Jack Dorsey's Block uses a multisig setup for added security.
Are hardware wallets hack-proof?
Like any device, hardware wallets can be compromised—something that became painfully apparent in July 2026, when attackers took advantage of a five-year-old Coldcard firmware bug that had weakened the randomness used to create seeds.
According to TRM Labs, the exploit drained about 1,816 BTC, worth around $116 million, from more than 5,200 addresses. Updating the firmware doesn't fix seeds that were already created, so affected users have to move their funds to a new wallet.
Hardware wallets are also vulnerable to physical hacks. In October 2026, Ledger revealed that an unauthorized chip implanted in devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis was able to read seed phrases as they were entered during setup and transmit them to an attacker. The investigation followed reports that some $86 million had been drained from Ledger wallet users.
Although the firm’s own Secure Element hardware had not been compromised, its reseller network created a centralized point of vulnerability that attackers were able to exploit by tampering with the device to add their own hidden chip.
Ledger subsequently halted distribution via resellers in seven Asian markets, while a European reseller, MediaMarkt, also stopped sales following reports of unauthorized implants. Rival manufacturer Trezor also wound up its reseller program as a “precautionary measure.”
Another point of vulnerability is third-party vendors and shipping partners, with several hacks and exploits exposing customer data including addresses. While no funds were lost in those cases, leaked customer details feed phishing scams and even physical "wrench attacks," where criminals threaten crypto holders in person.
For most people, phishing and a poorly stored seed phrase are much bigger risks than someone hacking the device itself.
Where to buy a hardware wallet
Always buy hardware wallets straight from the manufacturer's official website, and avoid second-hand devices and unofficial marketplace listings. As the CryptoBilis incident demonstrates, even authorized resellers represent a point of vulnerability that attackers can exploit, and it’s likely that manufacturers will rethink their reseller programs in its aftermath.
The future of hardware wallets
Hardware wallets are turning into full self-custody platforms, and broadening their scope beyond crypto transactions. Ledger’s latest device, the Android-powered Atom, launched in October 2026, is designed around messaging, apps and agentic finance. The firm has even stopped billing its devices as “hardware wallets,” preferring instead to refer to them as “signers” to reflect their widening array of use cases.
Hardware makers are also positioning themselves for AI agents. In June 2026, Ledger released Agent Stack, an open-source toolkit that lets AI agents check balances and draft transactions, but not move funds until a human signs off on a Ledger device. The same toolkit extends those hardware-enforced controls to institutional treasury teams through Ledger Enterprise, with policy enforcement anchored in hardware security modules.
Quantum computing is another future focus for manufacturers, since it could eventually break the cryptography that secures crypto wallets today. Trezor's Safe 7, launched in late 2025, uses a post-quantum signature scheme to verify its bootloader and is built to receive quantum-resistant updates without users having to move their keys to a new device. The concern has sharpened since Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake warned in October 2026 that AI could break crypto encryption before quantum computers do.
The business has hit some bumps. Ledger had been weighing a U.S. IPO at a valuation of about $4 billion, but put it on hold in May 2026 because of weak market conditions. Meanwhile, the Coldcard and CryptoBilis incidents, and customer data leaks, have been a wake-up call for users, highlighting that a hardware wallet is not the be-all and end-all of crypto security, and should form part of a suite of self-custody tools and practices.

articles.title: Balaji’s Farcaster Takeover Sparks Backlash Over Bans
articles.text:
Balaji’s ‘Singapore of social media’ begins with a wave of bans
Network School founder Balaji Srinivasan wants to turn Farcaster into a haven for well-mannered techno-optimists. He had to do a bit of housekeeping first.
Balaji Srinivasan’s Network School has begun its reign over the decentralized social platform Farcaster. Its first order of business? An apparent wave of bans that has prompted backlash from members of the decentralized social network.
Network School on Thursday announced it has acquired Farcaster from Neynar, rebranding it as the Network State Protocol. The same day, several users said on X that their Farcaster accounts had been restricted to “read-only,” as a result of previous posts that broke its new rules.
“I know most of these folks. They shaped Farcaster with their quirks and wit,” said Kunal Gandhi, former India ecosystem lead at Eigen Labs. “Obliterating accounts from the get-go for past posts is pretty silly. Goes against the ethos of decentralized social.”
The overhaul is the latest attempt to find a sustainable direction for Farcaster, which is changing hands for the second time this year. Co-founder Dan Romero said the platform had 250,000 monthly active users in December 2025.
Balaji wants the ‘Singapore of social media’
In a post to Farcaster on Thursday, Srinivasan said the bans were part of plans to turn the reference app into “the Singapore of social media,” a positive-sum community of techno-optimists that operate under a shared code of conduct.
One of the first steps was to institute “law and order,” he said. “In the pre-Internet world, it was simply unheard of to run up to a stranger and start cursing at them. We’re restoring that offline norm online.”
“Much like how President Bukele jailed a small fraction of repeat offenders to essentially eliminate crime in El Salvador, we’ve moderated out the small fraction of repeat offenders that have been muted or blocked by many accounts to stop random attacks within this Farcaster reference client.”
Srinivasan said both humans and AI were used to go through millions of posts to determine those to ban, adding there is an appeals process in place for them.
Rewarding “pro-social behavior”
Under Network School’s vision for Network State Protocol, users opt into a “social smart contract” authorizing its core team to set the app’s rules. Its accompanying “Network Code” classifies violations as digital felonies, misdemeanors or infractions, with penalties ranging from warnings and suspensions to bans. The rules apply to past posts as well as new ones.
The code also promises rewards for constructive behavior, including teaching others, sharing projects and disagreeing civilly, although it does not specify what those rewards entail.
Related: Farcaster to return $180M to investors following Neynar takeover
Network School says an open-weight AI model will apply the rules, with some manual judgment calls, and eventually wants to warn users of potential violations before they post.
The underlying Farcaster protocol will remain open, according to the announcement. Users who decline the contract will have read-only access to the main app but retain their keys, funds, followers and post history, allowing them to move to another client. Srinivasan described this ability to join, leave or build competing clients as “decentralized democracy.”
The eventual ambition extends beyond social media. Network School said its goal is for the online community to take physical form through meetups and pop-up events, ultimately developing into startup cities and network states.
Network School’s acquisition of Farcaster comes months after Malaysian authorities revoked its Forest City business licence and ordered it to cease operations, citing alleged licensing and premises-use violations. Srinivasan subsequently announced an agreement to establish a campus in Kazakhstan.

articles.title: Only 18% of Uniswap v3 positions under $1,000 beat holding after gas, study finds
articles.text:
Quick Take
- In eight sampled Ethereum v3 pools, 18% of closed regular positions below $1,000 beat holding after gas.
- V4 nets token transfers while standard pools retain inventory changes and stop earning swap fees outside their price ranges.
- VolatilePair Hook launched after the study cutoff, leaving a live test of how changing fees affect LP returns.
Gas charges tipped many small Uniswap liquidity positions behind simply holding the tokens, according to blockchain data firm Bitquery’s October 16 study. Among closed regular positions below $1,000 in eight sampled Ethereum v3 pools, 51% finished ahead before gas, compared with 18% afterward. The median gas bill for that group was 67 cents.
Uniswap v4’s flash accounting can reduce transfer overhead for liquidity providers, or LPs, who supply tokens for traders to swap. Standard v4 pools retain the price-range mechanics that change what a provider owns as prices move. Fees must compensate for those inventory changes as well as transaction costs.
Bitquery’s return study covers October 14, 2025, through October 13, 2026, in eight Ethereum v3 pools selected for their new-position counts in mid-2026. Its regular-position win rates exclude positions opened and closed within a single block.
Gas matters most to small positions
Across the return study’s eight sampled Ethereum v3 pools, 49% of 71,166 closed regular positions beat holding before gas. After transaction costs, that share fell to 34%.
The effect was particularly sharp below $1,000. A transaction cost measured in cents can consume a narrow advantage over leaving the original tokens in a wallet. Bigger deposits spread that cost over more capital, which helps explain why the before-and-after gap varies so much by position size.
Bitquery’s published size breakdown shows the pattern:
| Deposit size | Beat holding before gas | Beat holding after gas | 
|---|---|---|
| Below $1,000 | 51% | 18% | 
| $1,000–$10,000 | 45% | 36% | 
| $10,000–$100,000 | 50% | 45% | 
| $100,000–$1 million | 55% | 51% | 
| Above $1 million | 60% | 59% | 
Each rounded percentage describes how often a closed regular position beat the holding benchmark. Win frequency differs from the dollar-weighted result: a group can have many small winners and fewer large losers.
For the smallest band, gas separates the two win rates by 33 percentage points. That makes even modest execution savings consequential when a position’s advantage over holding is narrow.
For closed positions, Bitquery compares the tokens returned, plus collected fees, with holding the deposited tokens, using the exit price for both inventories. Gas is then deducted. A position can gain in dollar value while lagging a holding benchmark that gained more.
The study’s aggregate collected-fee comparison, which includes positions still open at the cutoff, reports $41.6 million in fees, a $60.6 million inventory shortfall against holding and $1.4 million of gas. Those rounded components reconcile to $20.4 million behind holding. Open positions are valued at the window’s closing price.
Bitquery estimates that the pools generated $59.5 million in total fees, while the position analysis counts $41.6 million collected. The remainder comprises fees still unclaimed at the cutoff or fees that could not be assigned to a position.
Open positions are excluded from the win rates because their unclaimed fees are absent from the study’s event-based accounting. Another 207 positions with fee claims crossed between sibling positions are excluded from per-position figures.
Bitquery counts each transaction’s gas once and splits it across liquidity actions.
What v4 changes for providers
Ethereum transaction fees are paid in ETH. V4’s flash accounting can reduce the work needed to settle swaps and liquidity changes by recording internal amounts owed during an operation and transferring tokens for the final net balance changes.
That is useful when a route crosses several pools or combines a swap with a liquidity deposit. Intermediate tokens need not move repeatedly between separate pool contracts when their obligations can be offset internally.
The saving depends on the transaction route and integration. A provider combining several operations may avoid more intermediate transfers than one making a simpler transaction.
Uniswap’s concentrated-liquidity documentation says v4 retains the same core implementation introduced in v3. Providers choose a price range for their capital. As swaps move the price, the quantities of the two tokens change; beyond a range boundary, a position consists entirely of one asset.
Outside its range, that liquidity stops earning swap fees. It can become active again if the price returns.
A provider can therefore save gas and still finish behind holding if the inventory gap exceeds fee income.
Bitquery’s v3–v4 activity study, corrected October 15, covers July 15 through October 13. It reports v4 liquidity adds rising from about 1,288 per day in the first week to 4,474 in the last, roughly 3.5 times. V3 remained near 1,300 per day.
The corrected comparison excludes zero-size events from both versions. Additions exceeded removals on 88 of 91 days for v4 and 89 for v3. An action count records how often liquidity moves, however, without showing the dollars added or withdrawn.
The standard position-manager route accounted for 77% of v4’s add-count growth. Its users include bots and token launchers alongside other wallets.
The study identifies 3,074 transaction-sending wallets active on both versions, compared with 18 when counted by the contracts calling pools. These are address counts rather than counts of people.
Because v4’s fee records differ from v3’s, Bitquery confines that comparison to liquidity behavior; it does not measure matched v3–v4 position returns.
Dynamic fees face a separate return test
V4 also allows optional hooks that customize pool behavior, including fees, accounting and pricing curves. Those changes can affect economics beyond transfer costs, so standard concentrated-liquidity mechanics cannot determine every hooked pool’s result.
On October 14, Uniswap Labs announced VolatilePair Hook live on Ethereum, starting with ETH/USDC. Its description says separate buying and selling fees are recalculated on each swap using recent price movements.
The hook launched after Bitquery’s October 13 observation cutoff, so it falls outside the study window.
CryptoSlate’s October 1 StablePair analysis examined a related distinction: fee rules can change trading income while providers remain exposed to the tokens they hold. The new v3 figures add a concrete position-size dimension to that problem.
V4 can reduce the transfer bill. Whether a provider beats holding depends on the inventory returned, fees earned and gas paid over the position’s life.

articles.title: MSCI’s new rules could squeeze Strategy’s Bitcoin buying machine
articles.text:
Quick Take
- MSCI adopted new eligibility rules for non-operating companies; the final affected constituents will be announced on Nov. 11.
- A November 2025 JPMorgan scenario estimated $2.8 billion in MSTR selling if MSCI removed Strategy.
- A smaller MSTR premium could make common-stock funding for Bitcoin purchases less attractive.
MSCI approved rules threatening Strategy's index membership as its shares trade nearly 69% below their peak.
On Oct. 15, the global index provider announced that it would adopt a new methodology excluding companies classified as non-operating businesses from its Global Investable Market Indexes. The changes take effect after the Nov. 30 market close, with the final list of affected companies scheduled for Nov. 11.
The decision puts Michael Saylor's Bitcoin treasury company at risk of losing access to billions of dollars in index-linked investment at a time when its stock has suffered one of its deepest declines since it adopted Bitcoin as its primary treasury asset in 2020.
Strategy's MSTR faces MSCI threat
MSCI had already identified Strategy, Japan's Metaplanet and uranium investment company Yellow Cake for potential deletion in an August simulation using May financial data. Ethereum treasury company SharpLink was also among three firms placed on a proposed watchlist.
MSCI will first assess whether a company has substantial operating assets. Companies that fail this initial screen will face five financial-ratio tests; being flagged on at least four makes them ineligible. Existing constituents must fail the eligibility screen in both of their two most recent annual filing periods before removal. MSCI may also use the most recent interim filing.
The framework replaces interim restrictions targeting companies whose digital assets represented at least 50% of their total assets. MSCI had abandoned an earlier outright exclusion proposal in January before expanding its review to businesses whose activities resemble investment vehicles.
For Strategy, the decision revives a threat that executives had spent months challenging. In September, the company argued that excluding Bitcoin treasury businesses would undermine MSCI's neutrality and impose an arbitrary distinction between operating companies and investment vehicles.
A chart shared by market commentator Mark Harvey, based on Yahoo Finance daily closing prices, puts MSTR 68.7% below its running high over the period shown. It also shows a drawdown exceeding 80% earlier in 2026 and a previous low of 89.3% below the running high.
Harvey described the depressed valuation as a generational buying opportunity, reflecting expectations that the company's long-term Bitcoin exposure could outweigh its current difficulties.
JPMorgan analysts estimated in November 2025 that MSCI removal could trigger approximately $2.8 billion in passive selling of MSTR shares.
Strategy's Bitcoin financing model faces another test
Market observers disagree over how severely MSCI-related selling would affect Strategy, particularly given the stock's substantial trading volume.
Bitcoin analyst Adrian Morris argued that predictions of a destabilizing selloff overlook the liquidity available in MSTR shares.
According to figures he shared, Strategy generated approximately $565.25 billion in dollar trading volume this year, averaging $2.91 billion daily and $13.79 billion weekly. Trading volume reached $15.29 billion during the week ending Oct. 9.
At those levels, JPMorgan's $2.8 billion selling scenario would represent approximately 96% of one average trading day's volume, 18.3% of the previous week's trading and just 0.5% of year-to-date turnover.
Morris said these figures suggest that index-related selling could be absorbed through normal trading activity and scheduled portfolio rebalancing without creating an existential liquidity problem.
His assessment broadly aligns with Strategy's September submission to MSCI, which estimated that funds tracking the provider's indexes held around 13 million MSTR shares, equivalent to just 3.1% of its basic shares outstanding.
That exposure represented approximately 60% of Strategy's average daily share trading volume over the preceding 30 days, according to the company.
The immediate effect would depend on demand for MSTR shares during the rebalancing period, particularly if investors adjusted positions ahead of the formal exclusion.
Nic Puckrin, CEO of Coin Bureau, identified a potentially larger risk involving Strategy's ability to finance future Bitcoin purchases.
He warned that sustained selling could compress the premium at which MSTR trades relative to the value of its Bitcoin holdings, weakening a mechanism that has supported the company's aggressive accumulation strategy.
Strategy has historically benefited from issuing common stock at valuations above its underlying Bitcoin net asset value. That premium allows it to raise capital for additional purchases on more favorable terms, potentially increasing Bitcoin exposure for existing shareholders.
A sustained reduction in the premium would make future common-stock issuance less attractive and could force greater reliance on preferred securities, debt or existing liquidity.
In its latest disclosure, the company reported acquiring just 250 BTC for $21.5 million during the week ending Oct. 11, funded primarily through $21 million raised by selling common shares.
During the same period, Strategy spent $192.4 million repurchasing its STRC preferred stock, considerably more than it allocated to Bitcoin acquisitions.
The transactions brought Strategy's holdings to 848,250 BTC, acquired for approximately $64 billion, while its dollar reserve stood at $4.88 billion. The company also reported an additional $640.5 million in cash available for broader treasury purposes.
MSCI will publish the final constituent changes on Nov. 11. If Strategy is removed, index-tracking funds would rebalance for implementation at the Nov. 30 close.

articles.title: MSCI Adopts Rules That Could Exclude Strategy
articles.text:
MSCI adopts index exclusion rules that could oust Strategy
Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi were previously identified for deletion under the methodology, with MSCI set to announce its final list on Nov. 11.
Index provider MSCI has adopted new rules that could lead to Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi being removed from its global indexes, while leaving several other crypto treasury companies facing potential exclusion.
MSCI said Thursday it will adopt a methodology proposed in August that would make “non-operating companies” ineligible for inclusion in the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes.
MSCI previously identified Strategy (MSTR) among the companies that would be deleted from the indexes under the “non-operating companies methodology.” Sharplink, Inc (SBET), Ton Strategy Company (TONX), Solana Company (HSDT) and DeFi Development Corp. (DFDV) are among companies that would be put on a “watchlist” for potential removal.
Removal could force funds tracking MSCI indexes to sell the affected companies’ shares, potentially putting pressure on stock prices and reducing passive investment demand.
“It removes a company from the default portfolios of tens of millions of people who never chose to remove it,” said Conner Brown, executive director of the Bitcoin Policy Institute in September, who was describing the consequences of broad-market index exclusion, with Strategy as the example.
Related: Strategy adds 250 Bitcoin as holdings reach 848,250 BTC
Under the new methodology, MSCI will assess companies based on their operating assets and five financial ratios. Companies failing at least four of the five tests could be deemed ineligible. Existing companies in the index must generally fail the screening process over two annual reporting periods before removal.
The final list of companies to be removed will be released on Nov. 11 and will take effect on Nov. 30, 2026, according to MSCI.
JPMorgan analysts previously estimated that Strategy’s exclusion from MSCI indexes could trigger roughly $2.8 billion in selling. That estimate concerned MSCI’s earlier digital asset proposal, rather than the rules adopted Thursday.
In August, Strategy opposed the changes but also played down the potential disruption, saying funds tracking MSCI’s Global Investable Market Indexes hold approximately 13 million shares, representing 3.1% of its basic shares outstanding. The company said those holdings amount to less than one day’s trading volume.
